title: 2027 Toyota RAV4 Raises Prices and Ride Height, PHEV Model Adds NACS
raw_summary: The 2027 Toyota RAV4 arrives with a collection of small tweaks that should add up to real improvements. Unfortunately, though not surprisingly, the new model year also comes with a slight price bump. The 2027 RAV4 starts at $33,895 in front-drive LE trim, $36,695 for the front-drive SE, and $38,095 for the front-drive XLE Premium. Adding all-wheel drive to any of those trims incurs an additional $1600 cost. The AWD-only Woodland trim is up to $42,250, while the XSE is up to $43,495, and the Limited is up to $45,495. Pricing for the plug-in versions starts at $43,695 for the entry SE, $47,650 for the Woodland, $49,395 for the XSE, and $50,695 for the GR Sport.

Every RAV4 thankfully now comes with a backup camera washer, and every AWD RAV4 gets Toyota’s Multi-Terrain Select modes. Plus, the Remote Connect trial is increasing from one year to five years, no matter the trim.

The bigger changes come when you zoom in. Woodland versions get redesigned all-weather floor and cargo mats. They also come with new suspension components, including springs, shocks, and jounce bumpers, that give them an additional inch of ground clearance. The granola-munching RAV4 now has 9.1 inches of clearance, compared with 8.1 inches for the rest of the lineup (aside from the GR Sport).

The plug-in models get some real changes, too. For starters, all PHEV RAV4s now come with a NACS charging port and a subsequent upgrade to Level 3 DC fast-charging. Interestingly, the switch to NACS resulted in Toyota relocating the charge port to the driver’s side of the vehicle. Plus, the onboard charger has been upgraded to a maximum of 11 kW on every trim.
The first of the standard hybrid models will start arriving later this year, with plug-in models scheduled to launch in early 2027.

Jack Fitzgerald’s love for cars stems from his as yet unshakable addiction to Formula 1. After a brief stint as a detailer for a local dealership group in college, he knew he needed a more permanent way to drive all the new cars he couldn’t afford and decided to pursue a career in auto writing. By hounding his college professors at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee, he was able to travel Wisconsin seeking out stories in the auto world before landing his dream job at Car and Driver . His new goal is to delay the inevitable demise of his 2010 Volkswagen Golf.

Most of the reason the Brick Shop team has managed to get the rollout right with a mix of obvious heroes like the Lamborghini Miura and secret-enthusiast-handshake cars like the Audi RS2 is down to close work with the designers at Hot Wheels. Located in El Segundo, California, the Hot Wheels team members are all gearheads of one flavor or another, and the passion they have for all wheeled things is genuine. Just, you know, scaled down for those iconic orange tracks.

Small scale is where you’ll find the latest Mattel Bricks sets, now built to the same size as the roughly 1/64th scale Hot Wheels themselves. They’re simple little cars, fewer than 30 pieces per kit, and at $4.99 each, they’re as dangerously tempting as an open family-size bag of potato chips. You can’t just have one.

The launch sets include a 2018 Audi TT RS , a 1991 Acura NSX , a 2024 Chevrolet Camaro ZL1 , a Maserati MCPura , a 1999 Honda S2000 , and a Bone Shaker (a 20-year-old hot rod by Hot Wheels design legend Larry Wood). The sets will be sold in blind boxes, so you’ll be getting a car at random when you’re buying them, adding to the fun. Launch is planned for January of next year, so you’ll be able to get your hands on one even if Santa pegged you on the naughty list for doing burnouts.

Even better is that these six tiny cars are only the first wave. By the end of next year, Mattel plans to have 20 models of 1/64-scale cars, making getting the full lineup something of a challenge for collectors. Even if you’re less serious about completing the series, one or two of these things are surely going to “accidentally” fall into the cart when you next go shopping for groceries.

Caleb Miller began blogging about cars at 13 years old, and he realized his dream of writing for a car magazine after graduating from Carnegie Mellon University and joining the Car and Driver team. He loves quirky and obscure autos, aiming to one day own something bizarre like a Nissan S-Cargo, and is an avid motorsports fan.

raw_summary: I recently wrote reviews of the new Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 and Explorer 100D . A few days later, a connection with Jackery messaged me that their Black Friday/Cyber Monday products had largely sold out. Just three days after launching on November 1. The recently launched Explorer 100D is still available in limited quantities at Walmart and Costco. While much of America was recovering from Halloween and election victory parties, portable batteries were selling out. This wasn’t the result of limited supply, but rather a massive, unanticipated increase in demand.

Between October 19 th and 26 th , Jackery retail sales increased 755% at Costco, 106% at Walmart, 297% at The Home Depot and 442% at Lowes. For added perspective, at Costco alone, sales increased from 2379 to 20,343 over that one week.

Jackery is looking into what’s behind the massive increase in demand. Clearly, there have been climate-related disasters over the past year, including hurricanes and wildfires. Jackery’s collaboration with the Red Cross helps illustrate the benefits of portable power in emergency response. However, that only partially explains the growth. A related potential explanation is the growing push for household preparedness. There are reports of at least 17 countries encouraging people to keep three to seven days of food, water and other essentials. Winter storm season, grid strain and rising energy costs could be stoking fears of potential power outages. The US FORTRESS America initiative has also added an emphasis on resilience. Together, these signals may be pushing “preparedness” beyond food and water to include power.

Preparedness is gaining emphasis with power becoming an increasingly important part of being prepared. The fear of “what if” can be a powerful motivator. Having backup power can keep the air handlers working for people’s furnaces. People on well water can keep the pumps running. Backup power can keep refrigerators full of food from spoiling.

Overall, Jackery is the global leader in solar generator sales volume and was named the “World’s No.1 Solar Generator Brand” by Frost & Sullivan. With over 15 years of experience and extensive safety protocols, the brand is well established. For the purchase of a product that manages risks, having a trusted brand is clearly valuable.

Although there has not been a detailed study of the consumer motivations, preparedness is likely a major motivator. However, versatile portable power stations have additional benefits. I keep finding new ways to use the HomePower 1000 Plus V2. And new possible benefits keep opening up.

raw_title: America’s New Shipbuilding Orders Are Expensive Bets on Fossil Freight
title: America's New Shipbuilding Orders Are Expensive Bets on Fossil Freight
raw_summary: South Korea’s Hanwha Group owns the Philadelphia shipyard that has become a centerpiece of Washington’s attempt to rebuild American commercial shipbuilding. Its Hanwha Ocean and Hanwha Systems subsidiaries acquired the US yard in December 2024 . The investment creates and sustains American production capacity and jobs while transferring shipbuilding expertise, technology and training from South Korea to US workers. The facility is in America, but its corporate ownership remains South Korean. The company’s published orderbook , however, tells a more complicated story: two liquefied natural gas carriers, four firm orders for oil and chemical tankers, and options for another six tankers. Three LNG-fueled container ships ordered by Matson in 2022 predate the current administration. The newer LNG and tanker orders come from Hanwha’s own shipping affiliates. They can help restart production, but buying ships from another company in the same group does not demonstrate that independent shipowners will pay US construction prices. The price gap is difficult to dismiss. Kinder Morgan’s January 2026 investor presentation estimates that a new medium-range Jones Act tanker would cost more than $240 million and require a long-term charter above $115,000 per day to justify construction. The existing charter market was around $90,000 per day. Kinder Morgan operates 16 tankers, with its fleet fully utilized, yet the gap between current charter revenue and the cost of a replacement vessel remains substantial. High utilization establishes a need for shipping services; it does not establish a financeable order for a new American-built tanker at today’s prices.

Its Hanwha Ocean and Hanwha Systems subsidiaries acquired the US yard in December 2024 . The investment creates and sustains American production capacity and jobs while transferring shipbuilding expertise, technology and training from South Korea to US workers. The facility is in America, but its corporate ownership remains South Korean. The company’s published orderbook , however, tells a more complicated story: two liquefied natural gas carriers, four firm orders for oil and chemical tankers, and options for another six tankers. Three LNG-fueled container ships ordered by Matson in 2022 predate the current administration. The newer LNG and tanker orders come from Hanwha’s own shipping affiliates. They can help restart production, but buying ships from another company in the same group does not demonstrate that independent shipowners will pay US construction prices.

The price gap is difficult to dismiss. Kinder Morgan’s January 2026 investor presentation estimates that a new medium-range Jones Act tanker would cost more than $240 million and require a long-term charter above $115,000 per day to justify construction. The existing charter market was around $90,000 per day. Kinder Morgan operates 16 tankers, with its fleet fully utilized, yet the gap between current charter revenue and the cost of a replacement vessel remains substantial. High utilization establishes a need for shipping services; it does not establish a financeable order for a new American-built tanker at today’s prices.

Coastal petroleum shipping also competes with other domestic infrastructure. A 2025 report to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission estimated moving gasoline from Houston to New York Harbor at under 8 cents per gallon by pipeline, about 20 cents by ship, and roughly 35 cents by rail. These illustrative route costs do not cover every destination, and tankers remain essential where pipelines are unavailable. They do show why expensive new tankers cannot count on charter customers accepting whatever price domestic construction requires. Longer term, the International Energy Agency estimates that electric vehicles displaced 1.7 million barrels of oil per day worldwide in 2025 and could displace about 5 million by 2030 under its policy scenarios. That does not mean US tanker demand vanishes, but fleet investment must account for changes in the cargo market over several decades.

LNG export carriers have a more plausible near-term growth market, although their prospects are different from the prospects of LNG-fueled container ships. US gas exports may expand, and LNG tankers will be needed to carry them. The commercial test for a US-built LNG carrier is whether it can win an arm’s-length contract against established Korean, Japanese and Chinese shipyards. Hanwha’s plan to train Philadelphia workers through its Korean shipyards can strengthen US industrial capability, and affiliated orders can provide an initial production run. The central uncertainty is whether independent buyers will still choose these ships once the group’s internal demand and any cargo preference are removed.

A broader domestic vessel market already exists. US-flag Great Lakes freighters carried 71.3 million tons in 2025 , much of it iron ore, limestone, cement, coal and other bulk materials. Those cargo flows will change as steelmaking and energy systems evolve, while ferry services, harbour vessels, inland cargo craft and multipurpose ships will still require renewal. Battery-electric and hybrid-electric propulsion offer practical options on routes with manageable energy requirements and reliable charging access. Large, long-distance bulk ships need a more selective technology assessment, rather than an assumption that every vessel can run on batteries.

Recent projects demonstrate what a committed customer can contribute to ship economics. CMA CGM, Nike and Gemadept launched an electric inland barge in Vietnam for a 180-kilometre round trip. Nike agreed to fill 90% of its capacity for eight years , helping justify a vessel reportedly costing about twice as much as its diesel equivalent. A dedicated charging installation and renewable electricity form part of the service. That is a commercially structured freight proposition, with its higher capital cost supported by contracted utilization and expected operating savings.

Electric propulsion does not cure the American shipbuilding cost problem by itself. Washington State’s three new hybrid-electric ferries carry a $714.5 million shipbuilding contract , and the state’s estimate including additional equipment and other program expenses is approximately $1.15 billion. Construction has started; the ferries are not yet in service. The path to a productive shipbuilding industry still runs through standardized designs, modular fabrication, trained workers, repeat orders, reliable delivery and falling labor-hours per vessel. It would be a mistake to treat electrification as a substitute for manufacturing reform.

Hanwha’s South Korean capital and know-how could contribute to that reform by developing US suppliers and production skills that serve several vessel classes. That is a meaningful way to rebuild domestic capability even though the parent company remains foreign-owned. Its progress should ultimately be measured by independent repeat customers, improving construction costs and commercially competitive vessels, rather than affiliated orders or investment announcements. A US maritime strategy anchored to the fossil-fuel cargoes of today risks missing a growing opportunity to build modern domestic vessels for the freight, port and ferry services of tomorrow.

title: Kia's PV7 electric van stretches over 17 feet and seats 9
raw_summary: Kia is expanding its electric van lineup with the PV7, a larger PV5 sibling that can carry nine people or a whole lot of cargo. The PV5, Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business, is proving to be a bigger hit than expected.
summary: Kia is expanding its electric van lineup with the PV7, a larger PV5 sibling that can carry nine people or a whole lot of cargo. The PV5, Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business, is proving to be a bigger hit than expected.
article_paragraphs: Kia is expanding its electric van lineup with the PV7, a larger PV5 sibling that can carry nine people or a whole lot of cargo.
The PV5, Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business, is proving to be a bigger hit than expected.

A year after it went on sale, the PV5 quickly became Europe’s most popular small electric van. In the first half of 2026, it was the top seller in its segment, accounting for 37% of electric C-segment van sales across Europe.
Next year, Kia will launch the PV7, the second electric van from its PBV business. Kia revealed the PV7 at IAA Transportation in Hanover, Germany, in September.
It’s based on the same E-GMP.S platform as the PV5, but the PV7 features a considerably longer wheelbase and stretched body, opening up more space inside.

The PV7 is over 17.5 ft long, measuring 5,350 mm long, 1,995 mm wide, and 1,990 mm high, with a 3,500 mm wheelbase. In comparison, the PV5 is just 4,695 mm long, 1,895 mm wide, and 1,915 mm tall, with a 2,995 mm wheelbase.
That’s even bigger than the Volkswagen ID. Buzz Long-Wheelbase (LWB), which measures 4,962 mm in length with a 3,239 mm wheelbase.
Like the PV5, the PV7 will initially be available in Passenger and Cargo body styles, but Kia plans to launch 23 different variants, or “top hats,” over the next few years.

Now, there’s a new Aviator PHEV in town, only this time, the towns it will be driving in will exclusively be across the Pacific Ocean. This is the Lincoln Aviator EX8, designed specifically for China and revealed via a regulatory filing with China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT). Developed as part of Ford’s joint venture with Chinese automaker Changan, the new Aviator EX8 looks completely different from the Aviator SUV sold on our shores. It’s handsome and confident, with a blockier shape and an upright front end, and the large rectangular grille is adorned with a series of cascading chrome trim pieces. A large U-shaped trim piece spans the base of the front fascia, giving the SUV a planted look. It’s about the same size as the Aviator sold here, coming in a tad shorter, about an inch narrower, and roughly an inch taller. The rear is simple, with just a full-width rectangular taillight.

It uses a 1.5-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine from Changan that produces 148 horsepower, but the MIIT documents didn’t reveal any details on the number of electric motors, their positioning, or their output. We can pretty definitively say that the Aviator EX8 will never be sold in the U.S., but we hope to see a hybrid Aviator return to our shores at some point in the future.

For my pick for this question, I'm going with something new to keep it interesting. The answer to which car screams "I'm divorced!" is the Dodge Charger Sixpack R/T — the Hurricane inline-six-powered Dodge muscle car. Specifically, it has to be the two-door coupe, because you're only seeing the kids on weekends, anyway. Why do you need easy access to the rear seats? Exactly.

The car has everything the modern divorced man needs: throwback looks to a time when their hair wasn't thinning, a big enough trunk to hold the toys they're going to bribe their kids with, and even a reasonable starting price at $51,990, including destination. Add in the 420 horsepower it produces and the fact it'll do zero to 60 mph in 4.6 seconds (fast enough to outrun your demons and the alimony payments), and you've got a winner on your hands. Of course, you could always go for the more expensive Charger Sixpack Scat Pack, but court was never going to let you off the hook that easily, so you've got to save where you can.

Anyway, that's enough out of me. How about you all head on down below and let your fellow Jalops know what cars scream "I'm divorced"? As always, I'll love you more if you tell me why you made your pick.

title: Too Much Motion in the Ocean: We Test the 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLS450
raw_summary: You can have the world’s best cartographers in your employ, and your ship can still end up drifting off course. The 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLS450 is one such boat. Mercedes has buildings full of nitpicky engineers whose sole collective life goal is to build the most comfortable three-row SUV on terra firma. And while the result of the GLS’s latest refresh largely hits the mark, we believe this ute’s ride quality missed its intended landing zone. Let’s focus on the high points first. We’re big fans of the base GLS450’s 3.0-liter turbocharged inline-six. Thanks to a stronger electric supercharger and a few other updates, this powertrain now spits out 375 horsepower and 413 pound-feet of torque fed through a nine-speed automatic transmission to all four wheels. With it, the GLS450 managed a solid 5.1-second sprint to 60, eventually clearing the quarter-mile mark in an equally respectable 13.6 seconds at 101 mph. Not bad for a gas-powered machine that tipped our scales at 5623 pounds.
summary: You can have the world’s best cartographers in your employ, and your ship can still end up drifting off course. The 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLS450 is one such boat. Mercedes has buildings full of nitpicky engineers whose sole collective life goal is to build the most comfortable three-row SUV on terra firma.
article_paragraphs: You can have the world’s best cartographers in your employ, and your ship can still end up drifting off course. The 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLS450 is one such boat. Mercedes has buildings full of nitpicky engineers whose sole collective life goal is to build the most comfortable three-row SUV on terra firma. And while the result of the GLS’s latest refresh largely hits the mark, we believe this ute’s ride quality missed its intended landing zone.

Let’s focus on the high points first. We’re big fans of the base GLS450’s 3.0-liter turbocharged inline-six. Thanks to a stronger electric supercharger and a few other updates, this powertrain now spits out 375 horsepower and 413 pound-feet of torque fed through a nine-speed automatic transmission to all four wheels. With it, the GLS450 managed a solid 5.1-second sprint to 60, eventually clearing the quarter-mile mark in an equally respectable 13.6 seconds at 101 mph. Not bad for a gas-powered machine that tipped our scales at 5623 pounds.

Out in the real world, the powertrain only ever feels smooth. Whether we’re stomping on the right pedal or just breathing on it, the result is the same: a muted little growl and plenty of grunt. The transmission stays out of the spotlight; in fact, everything hiding under the body does its best to stay out of earshot. Our microphones picked up very little cabin noise, recording just 65 decibels (20 sones) at a 70-mph cruise. Insofar as high-end family transportation goes, the GLS450 nails that part of its assignment.

The GLS450’s cabin also succeeds in its goals—mostly. The materials are standard Mercedes-Benz fare, with plenty of nice-feeling leather and vinyl up top, while most of the harder materials remain low in the cabin, away from traditional touch points. Our test car had the no-charge six-seater option; the captain’s chairs in the second row are cushy and make third-row ingress and egress a breeze. The car’s so dang large that even adults can be reasonably comfortable all the way in back, with decent headroom and legroom that’s fine for short jaunts around town.

However, our editors didn’t fully embrace the cabin’s centerpiece: the Superscreen. This panoply of digital real estate spans the entire width of the dashboard, with a single piece of glass encasing the digital gauge cluster, the primary infotainment touchscreen, and the optional (and wholly superfluous) passenger screen. It’s basically eliminated the need to design a dashboard, which does a disservice to those who appreciate an aesthetic other than Blade Runner Dystopia. In fact, this pixel addiction is a growing problem across the entire Mercedes lineup. But hey, at least the steering wheel picked up a physical rocker and a thumbwheel.

When it comes to the external half of the GLS-class’s refresh, the whole look gels, but like the revised S-class sedan before it, we’re wondering if Mercedes is going too hard in the paint on the self-branding. In addition to the gigantic three-pointed star on the grille, the grille itself now contains dozens of little three-pointed stars. Each headlight now has two three-pointed stars acting as running lights. In total, the rear lights contain six three-pointed stars. It’s a great design if you’re constantly forgetting what car you bought. Who are they trying to sell this thing to, the protagonist from Memento ?

The GLS450’s more prominent bugbear is its ride quality. Ordinarily, a plush ride means road inconsistencies disappear, replaced with a body that floats serenely over juts and ruts without transmitting undue movement to the cabin and its occupants. In the GLS450, though, it appears the suspension engineers were tasked with reinventing body-on-frame jiggle from first principles. On any road that isn’t obsidian smooth, the GLS suffers from an awful lot of lateral wobbling after tackling a bump, and the body barely settles down by the time the next one arrives. It’s as if the engineers benchmarked an unladen F-350. Our test car was riding on the stock air suspension, and while it’s possible that upgrading to the electrohydraulic E-Active Body Control system would eliminate these unwanted movements, we’re let down that this setup ever left the plant in Alabama.

Despite a terminal case of the Wibbly-Wobblies, GLS450 proved surprisingly sticky around our 300-foot skidpad. We managed 0.92 g of lateral grip from the Pirelli P Zero PZ5 summer tires (285/40R-23 front, 325/35R-23 rear). The GLS also stopped from 70 mph in a tidy 154 feet. We’d appreciate these stats more if they didn’t come attached to a four-wheeled waterbed.

title: Tesla hikes Cybertruck prices up to 10% after announcing it will kill production
raw_summary: Tesla has raised Cybertruck prices in the US by up to 10% and stopped taking orders for the base Dual Motor AWD trim. The cheapest Cybertruck you can actually order now costs $92,490. The move comes right after Tesla confirmed it will end Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027.
summary: Tesla has raised Cybertruck prices in the US by up to 10% and stopped taking orders for the base Dual Motor AWD trim. The cheapest Cybertruck you can actually order now costs $92,490. The move comes right after Tesla confirmed it will end Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027.
article_paragraphs: Tesla has raised Cybertruck prices in the US by up to 10% and stopped taking orders for the base Dual Motor AWD trim. The cheapest Cybertruck you can actually order now costs $92,490.
The move comes right after Tesla confirmed it will end Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027.
Here’s what Tesla’s online configurator shows today, compared to the prices set in August:
The Dual Motor trim still shows a new, higher price on Tesla’s website, but the option is greyed out. So Tesla raised the price of a version it isn’t selling anymore.

This is the second price hike in less than three months. Tesla raised prices by $5,000 on two trims in August , when the Dual Motor went from $69,990 to $74,990 and the Premium AWD from $79,990 to $84,990.

Add it up and the Premium AWD is now $12,500 (15.6%) more expensive than it was in early August. And the entry price for any Cybertruck you can order went from $69,990 to $92,490. That’s a 32% jump in about 10 weeks.
For reference, Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in 2019 with a promised starting price of $39,900.

The price hikes make little sense from a demand standpoint. Tesla doesn’t break out Cybertruck deliveries, but its “Other Models” category, which also includes the Model S, Model X, and Semi, fell 48% year-over-year to 8,295 units in Q3. We estimate Cybertrucks made up 7,000 to 8,000 of those, about 12% of the line’s 250,000-unit annual capacity.

The clip gives us the clearest look yet at the Cosmos’ lighting, front and rear, after months of camouflaged prototype sightings. But the car itself is still about a year away.
summary: Lucid has released a new teaser video of what looks like the Cosmos, its upcoming sub-$50,000 midsize electric SUV and the car that’s supposed to turn Lucid into a volume automaker. The clip gives us the clearest look yet at the Cosmos’ lighting, front and rear, after months of camouflaged prototype sightings.
article_paragraphs: Lucid has released a new teaser video of what looks like the Cosmos, its upcoming sub-$50,000 midsize electric SUV and the car that’s supposed to turn Lucid into a volume automaker.
The clip gives us the clearest look yet at the Cosmos’ lighting, front and rear, after months of camouflaged prototype sightings. But the car itself is still about a year away.

Lucid posted the 1 minute 34 second video on X yesterday. The caption talks about “elevating the experience of movement” and says Lucid can’t wait “to share this feeling with even more people.” It doesn’t name the vehicle, but “even more people” is about as subtle a hint at a cheaper model as you can get.

Two frames from the film show the vehicle at dusk. At the rear, “LUCID” is spelled out in red illuminated letters across the tailgate, flanked by thin red light strips, with a spoiler cutting across the base of the rear glass. Up front, a sculpted LED headlight with a row of vertical segments sweeps across a red body panel.

That rear end matches the Cosmos design Lucid registered with the EU Intellectual Property Office in May, which showed the same spelled-out “LUCID” tailgate and rear-glass spoiler. It also lines up with the thin red light strips on the camouflaged Cosmos prototype spotted on Highway 101 in California last month.
Lucid unveiled its plans for Cosmos and Earth at its first Investor Day in March . Both ride on the new midsize platform and start under $50,000, roughly half the price of the Gravity.

On paper, the Cosmos is impressive. Lucid claims about 300 miles of range from a 69 kWh pack, thanks to efficiency of up to 4.5 mi/kWh, which it says is 10% better than its closest competitor. It also claims 200 miles of range in 14 minutes of charging, and its new Atlas drive unit has 30% fewer parts and costs 37% less than the Zeus unit in the Gravity.
The problem is timing. Production was supposed to start in late 2026. In August, CEO Silvio Napoli pushed the Cosmos to 2027 , “most likely the second half.”

raw_title: This 1,000 HP Dodge Power Wagon Is Actually A TRX Underneath
title: This 1,000 HP Dodge Power Wagon Is Actually A TRX Underneath
raw_summary: The Dodge Power Wagon dates back to the mid-1940s, and while this example may look like an original that's been modernized, it's actually something else entirely. Built by Desert Power Wagons in North Carolina, it started life as a 2021 Ram 1500 TRX. If you want a pickup that looks like a classic but performs like a modern truck, something like this might be perfect. Known as Project Colossus, the Ram's chassis has been modified to support a third axle and two extra wheels. Those new rear wheels aren't just along for the ride and disconnected from the powertrain as we've seen on other 6x6 projects. Instead, this wild truck has a full-time BorgWarner transfer case delivering 6WD Auto, 6WD High, and 6WH Low operating ranges, plus a Dana 60 rear axle and an electronically locking differential. Known as Project Colossus, the Ram's chassis has been modified to support a third axle and two extra wheels. Those new rear wheels aren't just along for the ride and disconnected from the powertrain as we've seen on other 6x6 projects. Instead, this wild truck has a full-time BorgWarner transfer case delivering 6WD Auto, 6WD High, and 6WH Low operating ranges, plus a Dana 60 rear axle and an electronically locking differential. It also has Bilstein Black Hawk e2 active shock absorbers and Black Rhino wheels with 38-inch Toyo Open Country R/T tires.

The distinctive bodywork is the most significant change made. It features a four-door crew cab from Tisdale Coachworkers that almost perfectly mimics a classic Power Wagon. The front end is also just like an original and has similar headlights positioned on the front fenders and a brutish steel front bumper, now incorporating a heavy-duty winch. Adding to the truck's wild design is a stealthy Satin Charcoal finish.

We've seen builds from Desert Power Wagons in the past using Cummins engines from heavy-duty Ram trucks, but this particular beast uses the high-powered Hemi from a Ram 1500 TRX . In standard form, a TRX delivers 702 horsepower and 650 pound-feet from its supercharged 6.2-liter V8. That wasn't enough, so it's now been fitted with a National Speed Stage-3 upgrade that gives it 1,000 hp and 925 lb-ft. Key changes include a new camshaft, upgraded valve springs and pushrods, a larger supercharger, long-tube headers, a 108 mm throttle body, and an improved fuel system. The TRX's TorqueFlite 8HP95 eight-speed automatic transmission remains, and this wild Power Wagon also retains the TRX's driving modes, including Rock, Baja, Tow, Auto Sport, Snow, and even launch control.

The interior shares most of its components with a TRX. However, the tuner has given it a classic vibe with Rich Pinecone Distressed leather on the seats, door cards, dashboard, and center console. A JL Audio system has been added, along with a Rolls-Royce-esque starlight headliner. Not only is this insane Ram-based showpiece fully functional, it's currently for sale. The price? An eye-watering $599,950.

raw_summary: With just 3,800 miles on the clock, today's Nice Price or No Dice LeBaron Town & Country is a true time capsule of '80s glory. It even has a bench seat in the front! The 2013 Cadillac Escalade we looked at on Thursday is a hybrid in the modern sense, featuring a gearbox employing two electric motors to aid the V8 engine in both driving the SUV and keeping its high-voltage battery full of electrons. That was, and still is, a fiddly system with a number of known failure points. On top of that, our Escalade already had 140K under its belt, so those failures could be expected at any given time. Those factors led to warnings in the comments and eventually, a 65% 'No Dice' loss for the Caddy's $11,995 asking price.

In the 1933 novel "Lost Horizon" by James Hilton, a small group of Westerners survives a plane crash high in a remote, uncharted part of the Himalayas. There, they discover a lamasery—Shangri-La—which seemingly has magical properties that slow aging among its inhabitants. This comes at a high cost: the inhabitants are trapped there, because leaving means rapidly aging and dying. I know, bummer.

Today's 1986 Chrysler LeBaron Town & Country looks like it was just magically freed from some mystical Shangri-La, as it appears in as-new, almost entirely original condition and has less than 4,000 miles on the clock. How did this come to be? The seller has a succinct recap in the ad:

Back in 1986 a man bought his wife the finest station wagon Chrysler produced, this LeBaron Town & Country TURBO wagon. She only drove it 1500 miles before parking it in the garage when she became ill, and ultimately passed. The car ended up in climate controlled storage at a Chrysler dealer for 30 years. Then during Covid it was brought back to life with a new gas tank, driven a couple hundred miles and ended up on consignment at World Wide Autos in Colorado.

The current owner bought the car four years ago, brought it to Georgia, and replaced all the rubber bits, fluids, and the non-working factory stereo. Other than those updates, this K Car is claimed to be just as it left the factory.

This Town & Country has the goods, too. An unexpected decal on the hood announces the engine: a 2.2-liter Chrysler four with fuel injection and a Garrett T03 turbocharger. The motor was factory-rated at 146 horsepower and 168 pound-feet of torque, which might not seem like all that and a bag of chips today, but back in the mid-'80s it was pretty impressive.

raw_summary: The incredible news just keeps coming after Tuesday's huge victory for everyone not named Elon Musk . After a little more than three years blighting our roads, filling divorce court parking lots, and getting recalled for all of its parts falling off , the Tesla Cybertruck is dead. Never trust Elon Musk further than you can throw him , but early Friday morning, Tesla's CEO tweeted that the company will wind down production of the Cybertruck before finally killing it once and for all at some point next year. Posting at 12:30 a.m. Texas Freedom Time, a very normal time that every major CEO is awake and making important business announcements, Musk tweeted , "Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production." There's lightning in our veins, fire in our eyes, and soon to be a path of destruction in our wake. If we can kill the Tesla Cybertruck, what can't we do? Universal healthcare? Abolishing the electoral college? Free trans for everybody? Finally receiving a sincere apology from my mom? In 2027, we're making it happen.

It wasn't like it's that crazy for a large, generally established, electric-only automaker to add a pickup truck to its lineup. While a Moscow move may be coming, Tesla's a U.S. company that builds a lot of its vehicles including the Cybertruckkk in the U.S., so Tesla never had to worry about that pesky Chicken Tax. And us U.S. Americans sure love buying our pickup trucks. In fact, it should have been a hit. A U.S.-built pickup truck should have printed money for Tesla, but instead, it's dead after 3 horrible, painful, eye-assaulting years.

But it didn't. After the first blush of sales, interest in the truck fell faster than a stock price after a phony product reveal. The problem was, while looks are subjective, Tesla never bothered to make the Cybertruck good. I used hyperbole when I said all the Cybertruck's parts kept falling off. Technically that isn't true. But it's more true than it should be for a vehicle available for sale to the public, driven on public roads. Tesla's May recall over Cybertruck wheels falling off wasn't even the only recall Tesla had to issue over parts falling off the Cybertruck .

The Cybertruck also famously couldn't survive a car wash , got its butt kicked off-road by a Ford F-150 , had still more parts flying off on the road , oh yeah, snapped its frame in an off-road test . You know, good, old-fashioned American truck stuff. The fact that, by the time the Cybertruck launched, Musk had gone mask off as a full-fledged operative for the far-right , spending hundreds of millions of dollars to get Donald Trump elected in exchange for a role gutting regulators , didn't help either. It turns out people who buy electric aren't on Musk's chosen political side.

What's best, from a Republican perspective , is to crush EVs, see them driven before you, and hear the lamentations of the EVs' women. So they aren't what business consultants would call "the most reliable buyers of electric pickup trucks." Throw in prices being far higher after launch than we were originally told , and it shouldn't be surprising that sales were almost as terrible as talking to the owners .

raw_summary: McLaren’s new front wing, which will be the same concept it launches its 2027 Formula 1 car with, has been revealed at the Brazilian Grand Prix. As part of an end-of-season push by the Woking-based squad to deliver continuous improvements to its MCL40, the squad has brought its latest upgrades to Interlagos.

article_paragraphs: McLaren’s new front wing, which will be the same concept it launches its 2027 Formula 1 car with, has been revealed at the Brazilian Grand Prix.
As part of an end-of-season push by the Woking-based squad to deliver continuous improvements to its MCL40, the squad has brought its latest upgrades to Interlagos.
This includes tweaks to its floor, an updated rear wing, but also a front wing that will form the starting point for next season’s MCL41.
The front wing is a change of concept for the team as it features many revisions across the spectrum of wing elements.
The attachment point for the main plane and the endplate has been revised to now run across the lower edge – where it marries up with the refined outboard element.

The attachment between the nose and the main plane has been adjusted to sit on the second flap now rather than the mainplane, while the new wing also features an adjustment in the height of the flap elements.
Speaking ahead of the weekend, McLaren explained that the changes delivered were about both delivering more downforce and improving car balance.
Chief technical officer of aerodynamics Peter Prodromou also made clear that these changes were the launchpad for its 2027 project.

title: World's First Production Car To Cross 500 Kmph
raw_summary: You might remember BYD Yangwang U9 which debuted a couple of years ago as the vehicle that featured DiSus-X intelligent body control system that could perform rhythmic body movements (basically dance) and then it also stole the limelight by jumping in the air to avoid potholes, making the world gawk at it. Now, a more extreme version of this Megacar called, BYD Yangwang U9 Xtreme, has just made headlines as the world’s first production car to cross the 500 km/h speed barrier on open roads ever. Yangwang U9 Xtreme did it by clocking 503.17 km/h in Abu Dhabi, UAE, marking a historic milestone and has been awarded with a Guinness World Record.

Now, a more extreme version of this Megacar called, BYD Yangwang U9 Xtreme, has just made headlines as the world’s first production car to cross the 500 km/h speed barrier on open roads ever. Yangwang U9 Xtreme did it by clocking 503.17 km/h in Abu Dhabi, UAE, marking a historic milestone and has been awarded with a Guinness World Record.

There are sportscars, supercars and hypercars in the world, but BYD Yangwang U9 Xtreme is a Megacar, generating more than 1 MW of power (1,341 bhp). In fact, Yangwang U9 Xtreme is a multi-Megacar because it is rated at a peak power of 2,977 bhp, based on BYD’s 1200V e4 (Yi Si Fang) platform.

There are four motors powering Yangwang U9 Xtreme delivering 2,977 bhp of peak power and they can touch and bonkers 30,000 RPM. Combined, they deliver 1,200 bhp per tonne (power : weight ratio) and the torque vectoring system negates conventional axles and this system can adjust parameters at 100 times per second.

U9 Xtreme is a more performant version of BYD Yangwang U9 and it gets a host of updates in terms of aerodynamics to prevent it from flying, basically. These include a large carbon fiber front splitter, a dual-channel hood, tall swan neck rear spoiler and a massive diffuser. Yangwang U9 Xtreme gets unique graphics too and production is limited to just 30 units worldwide.

Last year in September, Yangwang U9 Xtreme locked 496.22 km/h top speed at Germany and then it clocked a sub 7 minutes lap time at Nurburgring Nordschleife (6m 59.157s), becoming the first mass produced electric supercar to achieve it. The new record was achieved at Abu Dhabi, UAE and it outdid itself by 6.95 km/h breaking the 500 km/h barrier at 503.17 km/h top speed.

Powering BYD Yangwang U9 Xtreme is an 80 kWh battery pack featuring a 30C discharge rate, this allows the battery to send enough juice across the 1200V and 1000A architecture to power four motors rated at 2,977 bhp.

In the video, we can see the professional driver warming up the tyres and increasing grip and traction for around a minute. And then he maintained the throttle around mid position till the vehicle reached 380 km/h and then he gunned it with full pedal to the metal till Yangwang U9 Xtreme hit 503.17 km/h top speed.

title: Liebherr expands excavator range with new, 250-tonne electric model
raw_summary: It takes some seriously heavy equipment to make an ultra-class mining truck look little , but that’s exactly what German equipment giant Liebherr does best, and its newest, 250-tonne production excavator keeps that tradition alive – only this time, it’s electric. Liebherr began converting its diesel-powered mining excavators to electric in limited numbers back in 2024 , and electric power has proven to be effective – moving millions of tons of dirt while saving millions of dollars in fuel and maintenance costs . Now, the company is translating that testing experience into regular production practice with the launch of a new, all-electric machine. Meet the R 9300 G8-E.
summary: It takes some seriously heavy equipment to make an ultra-class mining truck look little , but that’s exactly what German equipment giant Liebherr does best, and its newest, 250-tonne production excavator keeps that tradition alive – only this time, it’s electric.
article_paragraphs: It takes some seriously heavy equipment to make an ultra-class mining truck look little , but that’s exactly what German equipment giant Liebherr does best, and its newest, 250-tonne production excavator keeps that tradition alive – only this time, it’s electric.

Liebherr began converting its diesel-powered mining excavators to electric in limited numbers back in 2024 , and electric power has proven to be effective – moving millions of tons of dirt while saving millions of dollars in fuel and maintenance costs . Now, the company is translating that testing experience into regular production practice with the launch of a new, all-electric machine. Meet the R 9300 G8-E.

Based on the proven R 9300 G8 platform, the new Liebherr R 9300 G8-E packs an 850 kW (~1,140 hp) electric drivetrain designed to IEC standards and supports 6-6.6 kV power supplies. The company says its electric setup offers customers the same hydraulic power and bucket capacity (1.8 tonnes/cubic meter, or ~1.5 short tons/cubic yard) as the diesel version.

All that electric power ships with advanced electronics and operator assistance systems designed to maximize both efficiency and safety while giving mine operators more data to work and plan with. Liebherr describes its take on ADAS thusly:

The R 9300 G8-E comes with Liebherr Power Efficiency – Hydraulic Control as standard, which adapts hydraulic power to suit the machine’s load profile, reducing overall engine load factor. Thanks to its Generation 8 electronic architecture, the R 9300 G8-E is compatible with a range of Liebherr’s IoMine technology products, including its range of excavator Assistance Systems, the semi-autonomous Bucket Filling Assistant, the Skyview vision system as well as the data visualisation tool, Data View. Customers also have the option of installing Liebherr’s autonomous cable reel solution onto the excavator to assist with cable management and support machine mobility on site.

Like its repowered cousins , the big electric excavator does seem to have on-board batteries, but is primarily driven and operated with grid power, reducing charging and re-charging concerns and enabling round-the-clock operations for as long as grid power holds .

Liebherr touts the benefits of new R 9300 G8-E’s quiet, emissions-free running throughout its official announcement, but doesn’t stop there. The company says its EV, which makes do with thousands of fewer moving parts in its drivetrain, can also reduce maintenance requirements and associated operating costs in certain applications and site conditions while improving workplace conditions for the people who work in and around the machine.
The electric drivetrain also reduces vibration inside the cab, improving operator comfort, limiting fatigue, and potentially contributing to a safer working environment.

raw_title: Marquez quickest as Qatar MotoGP weekend kicks off
title: Marquez quickest as Qatar MotoGP weekend kicks off
raw_summary: MotoGP championship leader Marc Marquez led the way in the opening practice session of the Qatar Grand Prix, heading Marco Bezzecchi by a tenth of a second. Marquez led virtually the entire session on the dusty Lusail track, and ended up on a 1m52.278s. He never fitted a spare rear tyre - but neither did virtually anyone else, with no incentive to use up any of the valuable rubber in the less-representative daytime session (compared to Friday afternoon practice, the sprint and the grand prix all taking place in the evening under the lights). Fabio Di Giannantonio was third behind Marquez and Bezzecchi, four tenths down on the leader. Pedro Acosta was fourth as the lead KTM, but his RC16 seemed to either fail or run out of fuel in the end as he had to pull over to the side of the track. Jorge Martin, who had withdrawn from the Sepang weekend last time out due to his wrist fracture from Phillip Island, had a livelier start here, logging 16 laps and placing fifth. raw_summary: Elon Musk confirmed that Cybertruck production in Texas will end in 2027 to make way for the Cybercab Tesla's CEO famously declared the Cybertruck could brush off an assault from a 9mm handgun at its 2019 launch, but now he's fired one bullet the angular pickup can't dodge. article_paragraphs: Elon Musk confirmed that Cybertruck production in Texas will end in 2027 to make way for the Cybercab

Tesla's CEO famously declared the Cybertruck could brush off an assault from a 9mm handgun at its 2019 launch, but now he's fired one bullet the angular pickup can't dodge. "Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production," Musk wrote on X,the social media platform he bought in the long gap between the Cybertruck's 2019 debut, and the first production trucks being delivered to customers in December 2023.

Cybercab is Tesla's fully autonomous taxi , a two-seater pod with supercar-like scissor doors and no steering wheel. It made its initial debut in 2024, was shown in production form this September, and began offering limited paid public rides in Austin, Texas, the same month. Musk is betting big on the driverless machines, as well as robotics, and that leaves less room and resources for the vehicles that made the brand's name. He has already axed the Model S sedan and Model X SUV, and a long rumored small Tesla never materialized.

The Cybertruck is only built in Texas, and while Musk didn't explicitly say the pickup would die completely, rather than shift production to one of Tesla's other US sites, the implication is that it's the end of the road for one of the world's most controversial utilities. That implication is backed up by another social media post, this one from Wes Morrill, who was lead engineer on the Cybertruck project. "Cybertruck was an incredible technology platform and lives on through Cybercab," Morrill said on X. "Thanks to everyone who contributed to making the future looking like the future."

And it's not hard to see why Musk felt compelled to pull the plug. He once suggested Tesla might sell 250,000 Cybertrucks annually, potentially rising to 500,000 units. The reality was rather different.

Just 11,586 Cybertrucks were sold in the US in the first nine months of 2026, according to Cox Automotive estimates, that number down 28 percent from the same period in 2025. And 2025's production figures were themselves down 48.1 percent from the previous year's sales. Total sales are believed to be around 71,000 in almost three years, and a good chunk of them – almost 20 percent of Q4 2025's output – went to businesses owned by Elon Musk.

The Cybertruck's brutal, angular stainless steel design was polarizing from the start, though some truck buyers loved how different it looked from traditional American pickups. Others were disappointed that the production truck landed wearing a sticker price 50 percent higher than the $39,900 Musk had initially promised for a base, single-motor, rear-wheel drive truck.

The exclusively all-wheel drive launch lineup started at $62,380 (including $1,390 destination), and topped out at $101,290 for the 845 hp (857 PS / 630 kW), triple-motor Cyberbeast. Tesla did eventually add a more affordable single-motor Cybertruck costing $71,985 in April 2025, but sales were weak, and it was pulled only months later .

The first customer delivery took place at Renault’s newly inaugurated showroom in HITEC City , Hyderabad. According to Renault, Hyderabad is among the leading cities in India for Duster Hybrid bookings, although the company has not disclosed total bookings received so far.

The first Duster Strong Hybrid E-Tech 160 was handed over to T Krishna Gopal, CEO of Eduzi Academy, by Francisco Hidalgo, VP – Sales and Marketing, Renault Group India. Renault says it had targeted starting customer deliveries within a year of planning the hybrid’s introduction, with the aim of reaching buyers during the festive season. Deliveries have now commenced around Diwali, following the SUV’s launch last month.

Duster Hybrid is offered in three variants – Evolution at Rs 16.99 lakh, Techno at Rs 18.99 lakh and Emotion at Rs 19.49 lakh (ex-showroom). It competes with strong-hybrid versions of Maruti Grand Vitara, Maruti Victoris and Toyota Urban Cruiser Hyryder. Here is our detailed drive review .

Duster Strong Hybrid E-Tech 160 combines a 1.8-litre Atkinson-cycle petrol engine with two electric motors and a 1.4 kWh battery pack. Combined system output stands at 160 PS, with power delivered through Renault’s multi-mode automatic transmission.

ARAI-certified mileage is rated at 29 km/l, with Renault claiming a maximum driving range of up to 1,400 km on a full tank. The company also claims that up to 80% of city driving can be completed in electric mode under suitable conditions.

Other highlights include frequency-dependent dampers, an illuminated grille and revised interior colour themes. Renault offers a 7-year vehicle warranty along with an 8-year or 1.6 lakh km battery warranty.

Alongside the start of Duster Hybrid deliveries, Renault inaugurated its largest showroom in Hyderabad at HITEC City. Spread across 7,000 sq ft, the facility can display eight vehicles and is the company’s 30th new’R format showroom in India. Operated in partnership with VVC Group, the facility is the group’s third Renault showroom in Hyderabad, where it also operates two workshops.

title: Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck in 2027
raw_summary: Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck next year, according to CEO Elon Musk, who said on X that the company will use the factory space to build more two-seater Cybercab robotaxis. The decision to wind down the futuristic, steel-clad EV comes after just a few short years of underwhelming sales. When Musk handed over the first few Cybertrucks in late 2023, he predicted Tesla would sell around 250,000 per year. It was supposed to be such a cornerstone of Tesla’s future that, before construction began, the company talked about its Texas factory as the “Cybertruck factory.” But Tesla has instead sold just tens of thousands — total — over the last three years.
summary: Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck next year, according to CEO Elon Musk, who said on X that the company will use the factory space to build more two-seater Cybercab robotaxis. The decision to wind down the futuristic, steel-clad EV comes after just a few short years of underwhelming sales.
article_paragraphs: Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck next year, according to CEO Elon Musk, who said on X that the company will use the factory space to build more two-seater Cybercab robotaxis.

The decision to wind down the futuristic, steel-clad EV comes after just a few short years of underwhelming sales. When Musk handed over the first few Cybertrucks in late 2023, he predicted Tesla would sell around 250,000 per year. It was supposed to be such a cornerstone of Tesla’s future that, before construction began, the company talked about its Texas factory as the “Cybertruck factory.” But Tesla has instead sold just tens of thousands — total — over the last three years.
Tesla is killing off the Cybertruck at a moment when it is trying to become an AI- and robotics-focused company. A big part of that is its robotaxi ambitions.

The company has spent the last two months putting Cybercabs on the streets in its hometown of Austin, Texas. With no major incidents to date, the company has said it plans to expand the Cybercabs operations to other cities, starting with Dallas later this month. (Tesla also operates robotaxi versions of its Model Y SUVs in Austin, Houston, and Dallas, as well as three cities in Florida.)

This is the third product Tesla has discontinued in order to fuel those greater ambitions. Earlier this year, the company decided to end production of the Model S sedan and Model X SUV and instead use the factory space dedicated to those vehicles to make Optimus humanoid robots.
First announced in 2019, the Cybertruck was a product that Musk had long obsessed over.
“Probably my personal favorite for the next product is the pickup truck, and we are going to just do an amazing pickup truck,” he said on one of Tesla’s earnings calls that year.

Musk promised the Cybertruck would be radical, inspired by the designs of cyberpunk sci-fi stories like Blade Runner . While that certainly bore out in the design, the company overpromised on the basics of the Cybertruck from the jump. During the now-infamous reveal event in 2019, when head designer Franz von Holzhausen cracked the Cybertruck’s windows with steel balls, Tesla said the EV was supposed to start at under $40,000 and have up to 500 miles of range. It achieved neither of those figures.

article_paragraphs: Chinese equipment brand Zoomlion showed up to this week’s China International Agricultural Machinery Exhibition with a new ultra-high-horsepower hybrid tractor that sets a new benchmark, offering more than 1,600 hp while cutting back on both fuel and fumes.

Zoomlion calls its new 9DX hybrid tractor a radical rethink of what a modern ag unit can be , combining the all-day pulling power of a conventional diesel machine with the efficiency, accuracy, and instant torque benefits of electric drive . The company claims its hybrid setup can reducing fuel consumption, emissions, and deliver lower operating costs, without asking massive industrial farming operations to walk away from diesel entirely.

The tractor itself gets a headline-grabbing 1,600 hp Zoomlion 9DX features an 800V hybrid electric powertrain and continuously variable transmission that delivering a peak torque of 7,200 Nm (~5,300 lb-ft) of torque. Getting all that power to the ground is a four track tank-drive system riding on Zoomlion’s in-house developed 762 mm (~30 inch) wide tracks that are designed to distribute the tractor’s considerable weight for maximum traction and minimum soil compaction. What’s more, the high-traction treads can push the big machine to hit a maximum speed of 40 km/h across grades and slopes of up to 12 degrees.

The 9DX also gets a high-capacity hydraulic system capable of delivering 636 liters per minute of flow (~170 GPM), allowing it to work with some seriously heavy duty implements like ultra-wide seeders and variable-rate fertilizer applicators.

The Zoomlion 9DX was one of several new machines at this year’s exhibition, which hosted more than 3,000 exhibitors and vendors – but the big hp numbers all over the show made an even bigger impression, leading AGCO’s director of global electronic and electrical engineering, Nicolas Meunier, to tell Chinese State news agency Xinhua that the country had moved on from producing mostly low-horsepower tractors to building some seriously large machines.

There’s no official word on specs and batteries, but the company has developed an 800V modular battery pack system for its other equipment offerings that can scale from 140-800 kWh of capacity while other top-shelf Zoomlion tractors featuring an ag version of Cummins’ 15 liter turbodiesel.
The 9DX tops off what’s sure to be another record year for Zoomlion , which is coming off strong early export quarters shipping into Germany, Australia, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

title: BYD's electric hypercar hits 312 mph, first production car over 500 km/h
raw_summary: BYD’s Yangwang U9 Xtreme just reached 503.17 km/h (312.66 mph) on a closed highway in Abu Dhabi, making it the first production car ever to go faster than 500 km/h. The FIA and Guinness World Records both recognized the run. It’s the all-electric hypercar’s second top-speed record in just over a year, and the one it broke was its own.

article_paragraphs: BYD’s Yangwang U9 Xtreme just reached 503.17 km/h (312.66 mph) on a closed highway in Abu Dhabi, making it the first production car ever to go faster than 500 km/h.
The FIA and Guinness World Records both recognized the run. It’s the all-electric hypercar’s second top-speed record in just over a year, and the one it broke was its own.
BYD announced the record on X this morning, saying the U9 Xtreme “has done the impossible” and calling it “the fastest production car on the planet.”

Abu Dhabi closed a 10 km section of the Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed International Road (E11), in the emirate’s Al Dhafra Region, for the attempt. That gave the team a 7 km straight. Marc Basseng, the German racing driver who set the car’s previous record, was behind the wheel again.

It took two days. Basseng maxed out at 490 km/h on the first day, per the FIA. After an overnight round of changes to the rear wing, damping, and tire pressures, he got to 503.17 km/h on his second attempt of November 1.

The previous mark was 496.22 km/h (308 mph), set at Germany’s ATP Papenburg proving ground in September 2025. That run had already pushed the Bugatti Chiron Super Sport 300+ and its 490.48 km/h from 2019 off the top of the list.

And it comes just days after BYD released footage of a U9 Xtreme crashing into a guardrail at about 280 mph during an earlier high-speed test. The driver walked away unharmed. BYD went right back out and hit 457.89 km/h on the next run.

The U9 Xtreme is the track-focused version of the Yangwang U9, the flagship supercar from BYD’s luxury brand. It uses four electric motors, each rated at 555 kW and spinning up to 30,000 rpm, for 2,220 kW combined. That’s over 3,000 PS, or nearly 3,000 hp.

CEO Elon Musk announced early Friday that the automaker will “wind down” the electric pickup at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of 2027, about three and a half years after the first deliveries. Musk says it’s to make room for more Cybercab production.
article_paragraphs: Tesla is ending Cybertruck production. CEO Elon Musk announced early Friday that the automaker will “wind down” the electric pickup at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of 2027, about three and a half years after the first deliveries.

Musk says it’s to make room for more Cybercab production. But Giga Texas isn’t short on space. The Cybertruck is short on buyers, and it sells at roughly a tenth of the 250,000 units a year Tesla built its line for.
Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production
That’s all he said. Nothing yet on how long Tesla will keep selling inventory or what happens to parts and service for existing owners.
Tesla doesn’t break out Cybertruck deliveries. It lumps them into “Other Models,” along with the Model S, Model X, and now the Semi.

That bucket tells the story anyway. Tesla delivered 8,295 “Other Models” in Q3 2026, down 48% year-over-year and the lowest since Q2 2021. With Model S and Model X production over since April, we estimated that 7,000 to 8,000 of those were Cybertrucks .

That’s a pace of about 30,000 trucks a year. Tesla planned the Cybertruck line for 250,000 units annually, and its latest shareholder letter still lists more than 125,000 units of installed capacity. So the truck is selling at about 12% of plan, and roughly a quarter of what’s actually installed.
The US numbers from Cox Automotive are worse. Cox estimates 3,519 Cybertruck sales in Q1 2026 and 3,744 in Q2, down from 14,416 in Q3 2024.

CEO Elon Musk announced early Friday that the automaker will “wind down” the electric pickup at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of 2027, about three and a half years after the first deliveries.
Musk says it’s to make room for more Cybercab production.

Bharat NCAP crash testing agency has just published the crash testing results of Mahindra XUV3XO ZNG and it is now the latest vehicle in India to score the prestigious 5 Star crash safety rating. XUV3XO ZNG comes with over 35 standard safety features including 6 airbags, ISOFIX mounts, ESC and even dedicated CNG safety features.

With this achievement, Mahindra XUV3XO ZNG becomes India’s first Sub 4m CNG SUV to achieve this milestone. Where ratings are concerned, XUV3XO ZNG was subjected to Bharat NCAP’s usual crash testing norms and it scored 29.3 / 32 points in adult occupant protection and 45 / 49 points in child occupant protection.

On Bharat NCAP’s website, Mahindra XUV3XO ZNG is not listed as a separate car which underwent a crash test. Instead, the crash performance results of XUV3XO are extended to ZNG variants as well. The PM CG MT CNG Family which now gets 5 Star crash safety rating include MX1, MX2, MX Edge, REVX Edge (O), AX5 and REVX A.

Mahindra XUV3XO ZNG comes equipped with dual-cylinder CNG storage solution that ensures that boot space is not compromised like it usually happens in a single-cylinder solution. It is commendable that Mahindra has also retained the spare wheel under the body and then the same performance as non-CNG Petrol-only counterpart.

Dr Velusamy R, President, Automotive Business, Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd., said, “At Mahindra, safety is a fundamental commitment that guides every stage of vehicle development. The XUV 3XO ZNG was engineered to excel across every aspect of the ownership experience, delivering ‘zero compromise’ in space, technology, performance and driving experience.

Its robust architecture is engineered to provide high levels of occupant protection and peace of mind on every journey. The 5-star Bharat NCAP rating is a testament to our engineering excellence and reinforces the XUV 3XO ZNG’s position as an SUV that excels across every dimension.”

title: Energica rises from the ashes with plans for cheaper electric motorcycles
raw_summary: The Italian electric motorcycle maker, which ceased operations in 2024 after entering judicial liquidation, has announced a major revival under new international ownership. And while the Energica name is returning, the company behind it is going to look quite different this time around. Perhaps the biggest change is where the motorcycles will actually be built.
summary: The Italian electric motorcycle maker, which ceased operations in 2024 after entering judicial liquidation, has announced a major revival under new international ownership. And while the Energica name is returning, the company behind it is going to look quite different this time around. Perhaps the biggest change is where the motorcycles will actually be built.
article_paragraphs: The Italian electric motorcycle maker, which ceased operations in 2024 after entering judicial liquidation, has announced a major revival under new international ownership. And while the Energica name is returning, the company behind it is going to look quite different this time around.
Perhaps the biggest change is where the motorcycles will actually be built.

Energica says motorcycle production is moving to Asia, while design, engineering, research and development, as well as responsibility for technical and quality standards, will remain in Italy. The new manufacturing setup is expected to significantly reduce production costs, allowing Energica to cut motorcycle prices by around 20% compared to its previous models.
That could be a big deal for a company whose motorcycles were widely praised for their performance and technology, but were also firmly positioned at the premium end of the market.

The revival comes after Energica was acquired by Energica Pte. Ltd. , a Singapore-based company backed by international private investors. Importantly, much of the technological know-how isn’t disappearing overseas with the manufacturing. Energica says its core engineering and design leadership remains in Italy, including longtime CTO Giampiero Testoni and designer Paolo Imeni.

The first motorcycle to make its comeback will be the Energica Experia , the company’s adventure-oriented electric sport-tourer. After that, Energica plans to progressively restart production of the Ego, Eva Ribelle, and EsseEsse9, eventually bringing its entire previous lineup back to market.

At least initially, those motorcycles will use their existing platforms, which should help Energica get bikes rolling off the production line faster without having to develop and homologate entirely new machines. But upgrades are already planned, including a new battery and improvements to range, efficiency, performance, and reliability.

Energica is also specifically targeting Europe, the United States, and Australia as it rebuilds its dealer and service networks. Existing owners haven’t been forgotten either. The company says service has already resumed and spare-parts shipments have restarted to dealers in several countries.

article_paragraphs: Launched in August 2026 at Rs 2.22 lakh for the standard variant and Rs 2.62 lakh for the E-Clutch version, both ex-showroom, the Rebel 300 had been awaiting detailed India-specific specifications. The wait is now over.

Honda has officially revealed the India-spec Rebel 300’s technical specifications on its website, revealing its power output, weight, dimensions and equipment as customer deliveries approach. The update comes after the first motorcycles began reaching BigWing dealerships earlier this month. Hat tip to automotive enthusiast Ajendra for sharing this update.

Honda lists the Rebel 300 with a 286.01cc, liquid-cooled, single-cylinder, fuel-injected engine producing 20.3 kW, equivalent to approximately 27.6 PS, at 8,000 rpm. Peak torque is rated at 24.5 Nm at 6,250 rpm. Both variants get a six-speed gearbox. The standard motorcycle features an assist and slipper clutch, while the higher-priced version adds Honda’s E-Clutch system.

This allows riders to start, stop and change gears without using the clutch lever, although gear selection still requires the foot-operated shifter. Riders can also use the clutch lever conventionally. The E-Clutch variant weighs 176 kg, making it 3 kg heavier than the 173 kg standard version. Both have an 11.2-litre fuel tank.

Honda Rebel 300 measures 2,200 mm in length, 808 mm in width and 1,125 mm in height, with a 1,506 mm wheelbase. Seat height is confirmed at 690 mm, while ground clearance stands at 129 mm. The low seat should help riders place their feet on the ground, although clearance over taller speed breakers will need consideration.
Suspension comprises telescopic front forks and twin rear shock absorbers. The motorcycle uses 16-inch wheels, with a 130/90 front tyre and a 150/80 rear tyre. Honda also confirms dual-channel ABS.

The equipment list includes LED headlamps and tail lamps, a TFT instrument display, Bluetooth connectivity, turn-by-turn navigation and a Type-C charging port. The TFT confirmation also updates our earlier description of a compact circular digital console.

Earlier buyer communications suggest Honda BigWing in Lajpat Nagar, New Delhi, reportedly received two Rebel 300 motorcycles on November 4, both said to be E-Clutch versions. Deliveries are likely to start in coming days. These remain dealer-level estimates rather than a confirmed nationwide schedule.

Honda has shared the first teaser of the next generation Avancier, ahead of its market launch in Australia. The new SUV is expected to boast a three-row layout and will introduce a sharper styling language. Furthermore, it will come fitted with the next-gen Honda Hybrid powertrain which is set to gradually replace the current e:HEV setup across the entire lineup.

The original Avancier was an Accord-based wagon sold in the Japanese market between 1999 and 2003. The second generation that followed in 2016 was a Chinese-built crossover from the GAC Honda joint venture, sharing its underpinnings with the previous-gen Acura MDX. Now, the same nameplate will be used for a new SUV, positioned above the CR-V.

The official teaser reveals the horizontal and vertical LEDs on the tailgate, flanking the simplified Honda emblem above the Avancier lettering. We can also see the sharp lines of the greenhouse, the integrated roof spoiler, and the slim headlights. The latter have a fancy starting sequence but their shape is reminiscent of the Range Rover Evoque, especially in combination with the contours of the hood.

The new design language is expected to be applied to future Hondas, such as the next iterations of the Civic and the Accord. As for the interior, the Avancier will likely offer a three-row seven-seater layout, with more space and practicality compared to the smaller CR-V .

More important than the exterior design of the Avancier is what lies under the skin. While the automaker didn't share any details about the specifications, the teaser video features Honda Hybrid lettering instead of the traditional e:HEV that has been used in electrified Hondas since 2020.

The new moniker suggests that the Avancier could be one of the very first models to adopt the next generation of Honda's self-charging hybrid setup , arriving in 2027. This promises to improve fuel economy by over 10%, while being 30% cheaper to produce compared to the previous system. The electrified powertrain is expected to be based around an updated 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine, likely inheriting the Honda S+Shift system from the Prelude coupe.

Production of the third-gen Honda Avancier will reportedly take place in Thailand. Besides Australia, it has been rumored that the SUV will also be offered in the Japanese market. Rivals will include the Hyundai Santa Fe, the Kia Sorento, the Toyota Kruger (Highlander), the Mazda CX-80, the VW Tayron, and the BYD Sealion 8.
