title: The Olds Calais Was An Indy 500 Pace Car Edition With No Pace
raw_summary: For as long as there's been an Indianapolis 500, there's been an Indianapolis 500 pace car. But it took until 1953 — 42 years after the inaugural race — for automakers to realize they could make bank by peddling replicas of the sedans, coupes and convertibles that led the field. Some of these lookalikes, cars like the orange and white 1969 Chevy Camaro SS/RS, and the the black and silver 1978 Corvette pace car replica , are blue-chip collector classics. Others, like this Oldsmobile Calais 500 , which is up for auction through Bring a Trailer, are rarely remembered. Oldsmobile reportedly built 2,998 Calais 500 commemorative pace car editions (confusingly, some sources say just 242), though none of them looked anything like the real version. The genuine Indy Calais driven by Rockford Files star James Garner, (there were actually two cars) was a special convertible version that Olds never offered to the public.
summary: For as long as there's been an Indianapolis 500, there's been an Indianapolis 500 pace car. But it took until 1953 — 42 years after the inaugural race — for automakers to realize they could make bank by peddling replicas of the sedans, coupes and convertibles that led the field.
article_paragraphs: For as long as there's been an Indianapolis 500, there's been an Indianapolis 500 pace car. But it took until 1953 — 42 years after the inaugural race — for automakers to realize they could make bank by peddling replicas of the sedans, coupes and convertibles that led the field. Some of these lookalikes, cars like the orange and white 1969 Chevy Camaro SS/RS, and the the black and silver 1978 Corvette pace car replica , are blue-chip collector classics. Others, like this Oldsmobile Calais 500 , which is up for auction through Bring a Trailer, are rarely remembered.

Oldsmobile reportedly built 2,998 Calais 500 commemorative pace car editions (confusingly, some sources say just 242), though none of them looked anything like the real version. The genuine Indy Calais driven by Rockford Files star James Garner, (there were actually two cars) was a special convertible version that Olds never offered to the public.

Also not available via your Oldsmobile dealer, was the real pace car's specially tuned 2.7-liter version of GM's 2.5-liter Tech-4 inline-4 that whipped up 215 horsepower to ensure it could stay ahead of the open-wheel Indy racers.

The Calais was new for 1985, and shared its front-wheel drive N-body platform with the Pontiac Grand Am and Buick Somerset Regal. It came with either two or four doors, both with a vertical back window style lifted from Olds' bigger cars, a hangover from the 1970s that looked about as modern as cycle fenders and wooden spoked wheels.

All pace car editions got the two-door body, and came dressed in red metallic paint with a silver lower body, silver pace car graphics plastered across the doors, plus another sticker on the tail, and a couple of badges. They also got a silver and red bucket seat interior that made the car look like it was built to celebrate a NASA launch, not an automobile race. And, after that, Oldsmobile seems to have run out of ideas.

There were no mechanical upgrades, and you could even order your Calais 500 pace car edition with that year's standard Calais engine, the 92-horsepower 2.5-liter inline-4. Maybe the 500 referred to its 0-60 mph time. Salvation of sorts came in the form of an optional 3.0-liter V6, which pushed out 125 hp, though that meant forgoing a five-speed manual option, and putting up with a three-speed automatic.

Motorweek took a Calais V6 from zero to 60 mph in 11.4 seconds, performance it described as "commendable." Which just shows how easily pleased reviewers were back then, after having endured a decade of cars with smog-choked motors.

This auction Calais 500 is one of what the owner claims were 600 cars ordered with the 3.0-liter V6, and shows just 13,000 miles. Its silver interior looks virtually untouched, and the exterior is pretty peachy, too. Only the grubby engine and deteriorated hood insulation lets the the look down. Our favorite detail besides that upholstery has to be the Auto-Calculator trip computer, which must have seemed incredibly trick back in 1985.

raw_summary: After Kimi Antonelli earned his maiden Formula 1 world title at the Mexico Grand Prix, Mercedes can add a ninth constructors’ trophy to its record in Brazil. summary: After Kimi Antonelli earned his maiden Formula 1 world title at the Mexico Grand Prix, Mercedes can add a ninth constructors’ trophy to its record in Brazil. The Silver Arrows have won 12 out of 19 grands prix so far this season, meaning they comfortably lead the championship.
article_paragraphs: After Kimi Antonelli earned his maiden Formula 1 world title at the Mexico Grand Prix, Mercedes can add a ninth constructors’ trophy to its record in Brazil.

The Silver Arrows have won 12 out of 19 grands prix so far this season, meaning they comfortably lead the championship. Only Ferrari can mathematically catch them, but that’s a tall order with a 126-point deficit.

Mercedes had a first opportunity to triumph in Mexico, but that required a 1-2 and for Ferrari to score no more than four points. This time, the gap means the Brackley-based outfit just needs to outscore the Scuderia by at least three points in Sao Paulo.
Across the opening 19 rounds of the season (discounting sprint races), Mercedes has outscored Ferrari by three points or more on 10 occasions.
The 2026 season marks the first time Mercedes has won world titles without Lewis Hamilton since 1955, with the youthful Antonelli stepping up.
“The championships with Lewis were absolutely incredible and rewarding,” team principal Toto Wolff said.

“I felt that we all were part of Lewis' history, of the greatest champion, and that we would look back many years to come and say, ‘We've been world champions with Lewis Hamilton’. And this is something I'm very much still thinking about. He is one that stayed relevant and is very much culturally relevant beyond Formula 1.

“So that was very, very special championships that I will have for my whole life with me, and this one is different. As I said before, for me [Kimi] is still the kid that hasn't even changed visually a lot.

title: How the collision course between Hamilton and Leclerc was created
raw_summary: At the end of last season, the question of who was Ferrari’s spearhead in Formula 1 had seemingly been answered by Lewis Hamilton’s difficult first year at Maranello. The latest fracas between Hamilton and Charles Leclerc in Mexico underlined that 2026 not only reopened the debate, but hasn’t yet led to one driver or the other decisively seizing the initiative.
summary: At the end of last season, the question of who was Ferrari’s spearhead in Formula 1 had seemingly been answered by Lewis Hamilton’s difficult first year at Maranello. The latest fracas between Hamilton and Charles Leclerc in Mexico underlined that 2026 not only reopened the debate, but hasn’t yet led to one driver or the other decisively seizing the initiative.
article_paragraphs: At the end of last season, the question of who was Ferrari’s spearhead in Formula 1 had seemingly been answered by Lewis Hamilton’s difficult first year at Maranello.
The latest fracas between Hamilton and Charles Leclerc in Mexico underlined that 2026 not only reopened the debate, but hasn’t yet led to one driver or the other decisively seizing the initiative.
This is how F1 drivers become the de facto leader. Forget what contracts say or the perceived grace and favour of a team boss, if you are the stronger driver the team will coalesce around you.

That’s exactly why Leclerc and Hamilton are determined to assert themselves at every opportunity. And it required a significant shift of the landscape on both sides of the garage to create this scenario.
The first was Leclerc initially struggling with the 2026-spec cars. While there was a stretch early in the year when this was exaggerated by braking troubles, that was temporary.

However, he’s regularly criticised cars that don’t reward his style given the need to engineer in a level of consistency to optimise the power unit deployment and harvesting. That’s led to him having to drive in a less intuitive way.
"These cars are making us do things that we've never done before in our career," says Leclerc.

Little wonder Alan Jones - who has died, aged 80 - became an archetype of the perfect racing driver for Frank Williams and Patrick Head as they jointly put the Williams team on the map out of nowhere. It was a status they formalised by winning the 1980 drivers' and constructors' world titles together.
He wasn't particularly rated as an obvious world champion when he came over to the UK from Australia with £50 in his back pocket, to race in F3 in 1970.
But he was a hefty guy in an under-powered formula and still he was a frontrunner for a few seasons in British F3 and Formula Atlantic.
His first F1 chance came in 1975, with Graham Hill's team and a subsequent ride in Harry Stiller's privateer Hesketh.

He showed enough for John Surtees to take him on for the '76 season. At the non-championship Race of Champions he foreshadowed his later form by leading and dicing with James Hunt's McLaren but it was a low-key season and Jones and Surtees, as two hard-headed individuals dissatisfied with their situation, didn't hit it off. Jones left at the end of the season, prepared to walk out of F1 rather than stay in that environment.
Which made him available four races into the '77 season as a short-notice replacement at Shadow after Tom Pryce's fatal accident in the South African Grand Prix.

The Shadow DN8 was a little overweight but well-balanced enough for Jones' talent to become apparent. His victory in the wet Austrian Grand Prix was something of a shock result but he was quick, consistent and combative all year.

article_paragraphs: Hyundai Motor India has introduced a Usage-Based Insurance (UBI) programme for eligible customers with Bluelink-connected vehicles . Announced in association with partner insurers, the initiative could help customers save on their insurance renewal premium based on their driving behaviour.

The programme uses vehicle data recorded through Bluelink to generate a personalised driving score. This score is calculated using driving behaviour from the previous three months, assessing parameters such as rapid acceleration, rapid deceleration, braking, speed control and idling.

Since the information comes directly from the connected vehicle, customers do not need to install an additional tracking device. They can view their UBI score, check eligibility and choose whether to share the score with participating insurers through the Bluelink app.

Hyundai India Insurance Broking (HIIB) will act as an intermediary, facilitating the sharing of customer-consented driving scores between Hyundai and the insurance partners. Insurers will then use the score during underwriting to determine potential benefits at policy renewal.

Customers whose insurance renewal is due within the next 90 days will be able to view their score and explore potential insurance benefits. A UBI score of 70 or above may qualify for benefits, subject to the insurer’s underwriting policy and conditions.

Customers with scores below the threshold can use personalised driving tips to improve their driving behaviour and potentially become eligible for benefits. However, Hyundai has not disclosed a detailed score-to-discount structure.

The potential saving applies specifically to the own-damage premium. It should therefore not be interpreted as a flat 15% reduction in the total insurance bill. The release also does not specify whether a lower driving score could affect the renewal quote.

The initial phase includes Cholamandalam MS General Insurance, Go Digit General Insurance and ICICI Lombard General Insurance. The programme will be available to eligible customers across Hyundai’s Bluelink-connected product portfolio, with upcoming insurance renewals falling within the eligibility window.

title: Driven: The Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Won't Make You Wait
raw_summary: The most shocking thing about the new Mercedes-AMG GT63 4-Door Coupe isn’t its 1475 pound-feet of torque or its 1153 horsepower. Or the estimated 2.0-second run to 60 mph. Or the flat cornering. Or the responsive steering. Or the drive modes that let you change how the GT doles out its three-motor grunt. It isn’t even the polarizing style. It’s that this car charges at at a rate of up to 600 kilowatts . That kind of power makes replenishing the battery almost as quick as pumping gas. Mercedes says its new GT will go from 10 to 80 percent in just 11 minutes. In a demonstration we witnessed, the car was still pulling 259 kilowatts at 78 percent state of charge. Impressive stuff.
summary: The most shocking thing about the new Mercedes-AMG GT63 4-Door Coupe isn’t its 1475 pound-feet of torque or its 1153 horsepower. Or the estimated 2.0-second run to 60 mph. Or the drive modes that let you change how the GT doles out its three-motor grunt.
article_paragraphs: The most shocking thing about the new Mercedes-AMG GT63 4-Door Coupe isn’t its 1475 pound-feet of torque or its 1153 horsepower. Or the estimated 2.0-second run to 60 mph. Or the flat cornering. Or the responsive steering. Or the drive modes that let you change how the GT doles out its three-motor grunt. It isn’t even the polarizing style. It’s that this car charges at at a rate of up to 600 kilowatts .

That kind of power makes replenishing the battery almost as quick as pumping gas. Mercedes says its new GT will go from 10 to 80 percent in just 11 minutes. In a demonstration we witnessed, the car was still pulling 259 kilowatts at 78 percent state of charge. Impressive stuff.

Of course, finding a 600-kW charger in the U.S. is another story. In Europe, these kinds of high-high-power DC chargers are increasing in popularity thanks to a growing quantity of heavy electric trucks. But even if you can’t find a charger that can provide more than 350 kW of juice, the GT63—and its less powerful sibling, the 805-hp GT55—can max that charger out for much longer than an EV with a 350-kW peak. As you might expect, both GT variants will come to the U.S. with NACS plugs.

The 2027 GT 4-Door can do this thanks to a thermal strategy borrowed from Formula 1. The car’s 106-kWh battery pack, which consists of 2660 cells arranged in 18 modules, is oil cooled. The terminals of the individual cells are where the heat really builds during charging, and by using a cooling loop that focuses on those terminals first, engineers can pump more power into the battery without damaging the cells. This method keeps temps stable across the entire battery within a range of about 9 degrees.

EPA ranges are still TBD, but we expect both the GT55 and GT63 to break 300 miles in maximum-range configuration. Wheels and tires will play a role as they always do, but we mention a max-range config because the GT 4-Door packs a couple of optional active aerodynamic elements to boost range. A hidden front panel works in concert with an extendable rear diffuser, because extending the body’s total length reduces drag. (It’s also really interesting when the diffuser extends several inches beyond the rear bumper.) There are also some moving elements under the body work that increase downforce, but those are more for corner carving than for hypermiling. And, of course, the wing out back can adjust to reduce drag or increase downforce, depending on driving behavior.

The higher-zoot GT63 also comes packed with all manner of newfangled suspension hardware. Hydraulic anti-roll control and air springs support multilink geometries front and rear. All the suspension components are aluminum, except for the two rear upper links, which are stamped steel. The lower-power 55 gets conventional anti-roll bars instead of the hydraulic ones. Rear-axle steer, which can turn the rear rollers up to 6 degrees in either direction, is standard.

Another clever addition is the use of aramid in the crash structure, a synthetic fiber you might recognize from its use in bulletproof vests. AMG lashes aramid rope (roughly the diameter of a hearty man’s pinkie finger) to the longitudinal chassis rails. In the event that the car hits a pole or a tree, the rope transfers the load to the chassis, and those longitudinal members crumple inward a bit, hopefully preventing the impact from involving the undoubtedly expensive front motor.

“Structural frunk” is a phrase we’re still getting used to saying out loud. The AMG GT 4-Door has a small frunk, yes, but it’s best used to store a charging cable or other small knickknacks you want to keep handy. Unlike your typical plastic frunk, though, this one is made of carbon fiber. The box bolts directly to the chassis, and it’s stiff enough that it boosts the torsional rigidity of the front end by 35 percent. It is also curved to direct airflow under the hood, so it has three purposes. (Serving as an ersatz beverage cooler does not count as a fourth.)

raw_title: Open Your Mind And The 2027 Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe Will Blow It
title: Open Your Mind And The 2027 Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe Will Blow It
raw_summary: Appealing to enthusiasts and buyers of performance cars is already hard enough with internal combustion engines, whether we're talking affordable hot hatchbacks or high-end supercars. As many automakers have been learning the hard way, it's orders of magnitude tougher to build and sell a good electric car to those same enthusiasts. They want their cars to feel real , with tactile sensations and character and emotion and all those other valid clichés, and few (if any) EVs have achieved that or even really gotten close. Now, the wizards at Affalterbach have done it. The 2027 Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe has unbelievable performance figures when it comes to power and speed as well as efficiency and charging, it has advanced technology features and F1-derived aerodynamics, and months after the reveal its design still has everybody talking, to say the least. Most importantly, it is absolute dynamite to drive – a grand slam, a home run, the automotive equivalent of an EGOT, however else you want to say it – and much of that is down to how it emulates a combustion powertrain, complete with V8 noises and shifts that will stretch your definition of "real."

As many automakers have been learning the hard way, it's orders of magnitude tougher to build and sell a good electric car to those same enthusiasts. They want their cars to feel real , with tactile sensations and character and emotion and all those other valid clichés, and few (if any) EVs have achieved that or even really gotten close.

Now, the wizards at Affalterbach have done it. The 2027 Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe has unbelievable performance figures when it comes to power and speed as well as efficiency and charging, it has advanced technology features and F1-derived aerodynamics, and months after the reveal its design still has everybody talking, to say the least. Most importantly, it is absolute dynamite to drive – a grand slam, a home run, the automotive equivalent of an EGOT, however else you want to say it – and much of that is down to how it emulates a combustion powertrain, complete with V8 noises and shifts that will stretch your definition of "real."

Head of development Oliver Wiech told me that even the most staunch anti-EV car enthusiasts, from people on Mercedes' own engineering teams to its dealers and long-time AMG customers, have been completely enamored by the electric GT once they've experienced it for themselves . Regardless of how you feel about its styling or its powertrain or its perceived gimmicks, if you go into a drive in the new Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe with an open mind, prepare to have your mind blown.

Full disclosure: Mercedes flew me to Málaga and put me up in a lovely hotel so I could spend two days driving the GT55 on the road and the GT63 on track at Ascari. I spilled a latte on my MacBook Pro on the first day of the trip, so if you see any typos in here, I blame the crappy PC I've had to write this on.

In many ways this car is the heir to the first-generation Mercedes CLS, particularly because of its sloping roofline that's the reason for the four-door coupe moniker, and thankfully the new GT is much easier to get in and out of than both the original CLS (which I own) and the first-gen GT 4-Door Coupe that this EV replaces. Even people much taller than my 5-foot-9 self won't really have to worry about smacking their head when getting in or fitting comfortably in the seat. Despite being almost two inches lower in height than the old GT 4-Door, its interior seems far more spacious, even in the back seats.

I settle into a sports car-like driving position with a low H-point and a great view out ahead; the rear window seems small at first but visibility isn't that bad through it, and the C-pillar blind spot is better than in my 20-year-old CLS. Progress! All of the cars I drive are equipped with the optional performance seats with integrated headrests, which look cool and are very supportive and comfortable, even after spending hours in the car. They have a heat function and adjustable bolsters and lumbar support, but unfortunately if you want ventilation and massage (and I do want them) you have to stick with the still-supportive base seats.

Aside from some flourishes like the center screen canted toward the driver and the surrounds of the air vents, the GT's interior feels much like any other new Mercedes EV, and that same feeling extends to how it drives – in Comfort mode, at least. This is an easy car to drive around the city, with standard six-degree rear-wheel steering giving it a tight turning radius. The cars we're driving have staggered-width 21-inch wheels wearing Continental SportContact summer tires, and even with that big rubber the optional Active Ride Control hydraulic suspension keeps the ride firm and sporty but never uncomfortable or rough. It's certainly much more comfortable than the last-gen GT , which had a horrible ride.

When still in Comfort, I try out the first of the three Race Engineer knobs on the center console, which adjusts the responsiveness of the throttle pedal. (More on the other two later.) The dial goes from 1 to 9, with 1 being the least-responsive and 9 being the most, and boy does turning it up all the way make a difference. In addition to adjusting the actual responsiveness of the motors, the physical feel of the pedal changes, giving you less resistance when you press it like when cycling through regen braking settings.

article_paragraphs: Alan Jones, who has died aged 80 after a short illness, could or should have been a multiple Formula 1 world champion.
The 1980 title winner’s shock decision to quit at the end of 1981 opened the door for Keke Rosberg to join Williams , where the Finn took the 1982 crown.
Jones was the first driver to win the title with Williams, forming a strong partnership with team founders Frank Williams and Patrick Head.

Born in Melbourne in 1946, Jones was the son of businessman and racer Stan Jones, and watched from the sidelines when his father won the 1959 Australian Grand Prix at Albert Park. The younger Jones repeated the feat at Calder Park in 1980 and remains the last Australian driver to have won the race.

Jones dabbled in racing in the UK in the 1960s before returning to Australia. After moving to London in 1970, it took three years for him to establish himself, winning his first Formula 3 race at Silverstone in 1973, the same year he took second in the British F3 championship in a GRD.
In 1975 he made his F1 debut in a privateer Hesketh, and when that team shut at the end of the season he moved to Graham Hill’s squad, then endured a frustrating 1976 at Surtees.

Jones’s career looked to have stalled until Shadow called, having lost lead driver Tom Pryce in a tragic crash in South Africa. The DN8 was not cutting edge but Jones became a points threat and scored his first victory in the 1977 Austrian GP, charging through from 14th on the grid in changeable conditions.
Ferrari sounded him out for 1978 but, when Enzo Ferrari signed Gilles Villeneuve, Jones was left with an offer from the fledgling Williams operation.

raw_summary: Honda Rebel 300 units have started reaching dealerships in India, bringing the cruiser closer to its first customer deliveries. Fresh images show motorcycles inside a Honda BigWing showroom, following our earlier report that dealers had begun contacting buyers about delivery timelines. According to the latest information shared with us, Honda BigWing in Lajpat Nagar, New Delhi, received two Rebel 300 motorcycles on November 4, reportedly both in E-Clutch specification. Their arrival suggests preparations for the first handovers are progressing, although a nationwide delivery schedule has not been announced.

article_paragraphs: Honda Rebel 300 units have started reaching dealerships in India, bringing the cruiser closer to its first customer deliveries. Fresh images show motorcycles inside a Honda BigWing showroom, following our earlier report that dealers had begun contacting buyers about delivery timelines.

According to the latest information shared with us, Honda BigWing in Lajpat Nagar, New Delhi, received two Rebel 300 motorcycles on November 4, reportedly both in E-Clutch specification. Their arrival suggests preparations for the first handovers are progressing, although a nationwide delivery schedule has not been announced.

The latest photographs show Rebel motorcycles in silver and black finishes, parked alongside other Honda models. Protective wrapping remains on the seats and some components, indicating that the motorcycles have recently arrived at the showroom.

The images provide a closer look at the Rebel’s low-slung stance, sculpted fuel tank and scooped rider seat. Black finishes across the frame, engine, exhaust and wheels contrast with the bodywork, while the separate pillion seat sits above the rear fender.

A compact circular digital instrument console, round mirrors and a wide handlebar complete the familiar cruiser layout. The low seating position remains one of the Rebel’s key attractions, particularly for riders looking for an approachable motorcycle for everyday use.

The dealership arrivals follow updates from buyers who had been waiting since bookings opened earlier this year. In our October 31 report, customers from different cities shared communications from BigWing dealerships indicating that first-batch deliveries would begin during November.

One E-Clutch buyer had been informed of a possible November 6 handover, while another customer in Bengaluru reported a delivery window beginning November 10. Other buyers had received later estimates, including November-end and, in some cases, January 2027.

The latest arrivals support those earlier indications of an approaching delivery rollout. However, availability is likely to vary by dealership, variant and booking allocation. Receipt of showroom stock does not necessarily mean customer deliveries have already commenced.

raw_title: 1980 F1 champion Alan Jones passes away
title: 1980 F1 champion Alan Jones passes away
raw_summary: Alan Jones, the 1980 Formula 1 world champion and first title winner for the Williams F1 team, has passed away after a short illness. Jones, who turned 80 earlier this week, was a 12-time F1 race winner and the second Australian driver to win the world championship, after Jack Brabham.
summary: Alan Jones, the 1980 Formula 1 world champion and first title winner for the Williams F1 team, has passed away after a short illness. Jones, who turned 80 earlier this week, was a 12-time F1 race winner and the second Australian driver to win the world championship, after Jack Brabham.
article_paragraphs: Alan Jones, the 1980 Formula 1 world champion and first title winner for the Williams F1 team, has passed away after a short illness.
Jones, who turned 80 earlier this week, was a 12-time F1 race winner and the second Australian driver to win the world championship, after Jack Brabham.
News of Jones’s passing emerged during the early hours of Thursday morning.
His former team Williams released a statement saying: “Everyone at Williams is deeply saddened to learn of Alan Jones’ passing.

“Alan was instrumental in making Williams what it is today, forming an extraordinary bond with Frank Williams and Patrick Head to become our first drivers’ world champion in just our fourth season in Formula 1.
“He set the standard for Williams champions: a fast, uncompromising racer with a challenger mentality who loved motor racing and dedicated his life to it.
“He is a true Australian icon and a Williams legend, and he will be dearly missed.
“We send our love and thoughts to the Jones family and all his friends.”

raw_title: 2027 Toyota Innova Hycross Facelift Confirmed For Launch On Nov 25 – Key Details
title: 2027 Toyota Innova Hycross Facelift Confirmed For Launch On Nov 25
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Toyota will introduce its revised Innova Hycross premium MPV on November 25 as road tests indicate styling changes and a host of interior enhancements Toyota has been testing the Innova Hycross facelift on Indian roads for months and the manufacturer has confirmed November 25, 2026 as its launch date as we speculated earlier. The MPV debuted in India towards the end of 2022 and is set to receive its first substantial revision. Interestingly, the Indian model could receive more extensive exterior changes than the recently updated Indonesian version which gained interior upgrades without a major styling revision. The existing Innova Hycross uses two petrol powertrains – both employing 2.0-litre four-cylinder engines. The naturally aspirated petrol develops 173 hp and uses a CVT automatic transmission. The petrol-electric hybrid produces a combined 184 hp and uses an e-CVT. Both powertrains are expected to be retained for the facelift. The current ARAI-certified mileage figures stand at 16.13 kmpl for the petrol and 23.24 kmpl for the hybrid. The test vehicles reveal noticeable revisions to the exterior mainly around the front fascia. The grille has a wider and more angular design complemented by slimmer projector headlamps and a redesigned bumper. Speculations also indicate pixel-like LED fog lamps, revised alloy wheels and altered rear lamp graphics. The side profile retains the familiar window outline, roofline and overall proportions of the existing MPV. Image Source: habeeb_payyoly The Innova Hycross already offers a considerable amount of equipment in its top-spec trims. The list consists of a panoramic sunroof, ventilated front seats, electrically adjustable seating and powered ottoman seats for second-row passengers. Toyota Safety Sense driver assistance is also available on selected variants. The facelift could revise the equipment distribution between trims alongside changes to the cabin materials and upholstery. A recent update to the Kijang Innova Zenix in Indonesia provides an indication of the possible cabin revisions for our local market. The Indonesian hybrid now gets a 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster replacing the earlier analogue arrangement. The top-spec versions also use a 12.3-inch infotainment touchscreen instead of the previous 10.1-inch display while the petrol variants receive a smaller 7-inch instrument screen. Toyota could introduce similar displays in India alongside revised infotainment software and interior colour choices. Image Source: OnlyNandos/Youtube The hybrid powertrain could also receive modifications for increased ethanol compatibility. Toyota previously demonstrated a flex-fuel Innova Hycross prototype capable of operating on petrol blends containing up to 85 per cent ethanol. The experimental vehicle used a modified 2.0-litre Atkinson cycle petrol engine and an electric motor. Reports suggest the production facelift could support E30 petrol or a higher ethanol concentration potentially becoming the first mass-market flex-fuel hybrid of its type in India. The revised Innova Hycross is expected to cost between Rs. 20 lakh and Rs. 35 lakh (ex-showroom) and tts closest rival will be the Maruti Suzuki Invicto which shares the same monocoque architecture and petrol-electric hybrid drivetrain. Toyota also sells the diesel-powered Innova Crysta In India but it will be phased out in the near future.

raw_title: Mahindra Scorpio N Edition One Caught Undisguised At Dealer Yard
title: Mahindra Scorpio N Edition One Caught Undisguised At Dealer Yard
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - The special edition Mahindra Scorpio N One gets a horizontal grille design, wine-red cabin upholstery and unique exterior badges Mahindra introduced a substantial equipment revision for the Scorpio N in August 2026 and backing it up, a special edition has now surfaced caught at a dealership yard. The black SUV carries Edition One badges, a redesigned grille and a distinctive wine-red interior. The interior is the biggest visual departure from the regular Scorpio N as well. Dark wine-red upholstery extends over the seats, dashboard sections and door pads contrasting against the black upper dashboard and lower interior plastics. Meanwhile, the seats have stitched surfaces and perforated centre sections while metallic trim surrounds the door handles, air vents and centre console. The second row uses a bench seat and rear air conditioning vents sit behind the front centre armrest. The Mahindra Scorpio N Edition One badges are visible on the rear pillars and front doors. The rear retains the tall vertical LED tail lamps, roof spoiler, rear wiper and sculpted tailgate of the existing SUV. The black exterior also has window surrounds, roof rails, side steps and dark alloy wheels. It must be noted that Mahindra introduced revised 18-inch diamond-cut wheels on selected Scorpio N variants in August. The front end receives the apparent exterior modification. Multiple horizontal black slats replace the vertical grille elements of the standard Scorpio N and small rectangular metallic inserts sit between the slats. The Mahindra Twin Peaks emblem occupies the centre of the grille framed by a bright upper trim section. The angular headlamp housings, LED daytime running lamps, sculpted bonnet, and lower fog lamp recesses retain their familiar shapes. Silver detailing near the lower bumper can also be seen. It boasts a panoramic sunroof, a large central touchscreen, a multifunction steering wheel and an automatic gear selector. The updated Scorpio N recently introduced a 12.3-inch infotainment display, a 10.25-inch digital instrument cluster and revised cabin controls. Moreover, selected top-spec variants also received a 540-degree camera system, Level 2 driver assistance and a panoramic sunroof. The Scorpio N uses a 2.0-litre turbocharged petrol engine and a 2.2-litre turbocharged diesel engine. Both powertrains have six-speed manual and torque-converter automatic transmission options based on the variant. Four-wheel drive is available on selected diesel configurations and the Edition One appears to be available in both MT and AT. Mahindra already offers the Scorpio N Carbon Edition which uses black exterior detailing and a dark cabin treatment. The Edition One takes a different visual route as the wine-red interior contrasts against the black bodywork and metallic exterior trim. The standard Scorpio N currently costs between Rs. 13.69 lakh and Rs. 25.49 lakh (ex-showroom).

title: Two Wheeler Sales Oct 2026 - Hero, Honda, TVS, Bajaj, Suzuki, Royal Enfield
raw_summary: India’s six major two-wheeler manufacturers registered combined sales of 29,20,563 units in October 2026, compared to 25,08,082 units a year earlier. This represents growth of 16.45%, with all six manufacturers reporting higher volumes year-on-year. Compared to September 2026, combined sales increased 2.92%. Hero MotoCorp led domestic two-wheeler sales with 7,05,084 units, up 16.58% from 6,04,829 units in October 2025. The company added 1,00,255 units year-on-year, the largest absolute domestic increase among these manufacturers. However, volumes declined 4.60% compared to September.
summary: India’s six major two-wheeler manufacturers registered combined sales of 29,20,563 units in October 2026, compared to 25,08,082 units a year earlier. This represents growth of 16.45%, with all six manufacturers reporting higher volumes year-on-year. Compared to September 2026, combined sales increased 2.92%. Hero MotoCorp led domestic two-wheeler sales with 7,05,084 units, up 16.58% from 6,04,829 units in October 2025.
article_paragraphs: India’s six major two-wheeler manufacturers registered combined sales of 29,20,563 units in October 2026, compared to 25,08,082 units a year earlier. This represents growth of 16.45%, with all six manufacturers reporting higher volumes year-on-year. Compared to September 2026, combined sales increased 2.92%.

Hero MotoCorp led domestic two-wheeler sales with 7,05,084 units, up 16.58% from 6,04,829 units in October 2025. The company added 1,00,255 units year-on-year, the largest absolute domestic increase among these manufacturers. However, volumes declined 4.60% compared to September.

Honda ranked second with domestic sales of 6,64,831 units, registering 11% YoY growth and 4.41% MoM growth. Hero’s domestic lead over Honda stood at 40,253 units. TVS secured third position with 5,14,764 units, growing 22.09% YoY and 6.78% MoM. This was the strongest domestic percentage growth among the six manufacturers on a year-on-year basis.

Bajaj followed with 2,92,885 units, up 9.91% YoY. Compared to September, sales increased 22.15%, making Bajaj the fastest-growing manufacturer domestically on a month-on-month basis. Suzuki sold 1,24,559 units in India, recording growth of 20.40% YoY and 14.48% MoM. Royal Enfield followed closely with 1,21,527 units, up 4.01% YoY and marginally higher by 0.17% MoM.

Bajaj remained the largest two-wheeler exporter in this group, shipping 2,08,309 units in October 2026. Exports increased 18.46% YoY, although they declined 1.61% compared to September. Bajaj contributed 41.92% of the six manufacturers’ combined exports.

TVS ranked second with 1,55,915 units, registering strong growth of 50.61% YoY. The company added 52,396 units over October 2025, accounting for more than half of the group’s net export increase. However, shipments declined 4.86% MoM. Honda exported 69,735 units, growing 35.03% YoY and 0.34% MoM. Hero’s exports stood at 29,319 units, down 5.36% YoY but up 7.28% over September.

Suzuki reported exports of 21,720 units, declining 15.84% YoY and 12.71% MoM. Royal Enfield shipped 11,915 motorcycles, registering 46.97% YoY growth, although volumes fell 5.68% MoM. Combined exports stood at 4,96,913 units, growing 25.51% YoY but declining 2.56% compared to September.

Including domestic sales and exports, Honda finished October with 7,34,566 units, narrowly ahead of Hero’s 7,34,403 units. The difference was just 163 units, with both manufacturers accounting for approximately 25.15% each of the combined total.

raw_title: Hyundai Ioniq P Name Trademarked, To Likely Be Used For Upcoming Small EV
title: Hyundai Ioniq P Name Trademarked, To Likely Be Used For Upcoming Small EV
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - The India-developed Hyundai compact electric SUV could utilise the Ioniq P name ahead of its expected debut soon Hyundai has confirmed plans for a compact electric SUV developed specifically for India and its production name could now be taking shape. At a recent earnings call, Hyundai management mentioned the Ioniq P for the Indian market and the company has now filed a trademark application for the name under Class 12 which relates to automobiles and associated components. However, Hyundai has not formally identified the upcoming HE1i project as Ioniq P just yet. The forthcoming electric SUV will sit below the Creta Electric and is expected to become the least expensive electric car in the Hyundai India portfolio. The model will compete against the Tata Nexon EV, Mahindra XUV 3XO EV and Kia Syros EV amongst others. The HE1i has been developed as a standalone electric vehicle instead of an electric derivative of any existing ICE offering from the brand. The camouflaged test vehicles reveal an upright front fascia, a nearly flat roof and squared-off body proportions. The front features slim LED daytime running lamps positioned above the main headlamp units. The side profile shows prominent roof rails, short overhangs and dual-tone alloy wheels. The tall cabin and relatively straight roofline distinguish the SUV from the more rounded Creta Electric. Representational The electric SUV is slated for production at the Hyundai factory in Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu. Initial vehicles will use imported battery cells sourced from Svolt after delays at the domestic cell manufacturing facility of Exide Industries. Hyundai plans to source locally manufactured cells from Exide at a later stage but prices are expected to be competitive right from the get-go. The manufacturer has already confirmed next generation infotainment system and Level 2 driver assistance for the India-specific electric SUV as both technologies were announced at the 2026 CEO Investor Day. Hyundai has also invested in local development and component sourcing for the project which is intended to serve the domestic compact electric SUV segment as well as possible international markets. Hyundai Inster It is no secret that the HE1i will use the E-GMP (K) architecture which also employed by the Hyundai Inster sold internationally. Two battery configurations are expected consisting of standard range and long range options. The overseas Inster uses 42 kWh and 49 kWh batteries and we expect the Ioniq P to share at least one battery with the recently introduced Syros EV. The new electric SUV is scheduled to debut next month and its prices will be announced soon after. The company expects electric vehicles to contribute more than 7 per cent of its domestic sales within the next year compared to 1 per cent in FY26. The HE1i will be Hyundai’s first locally developed electric SUV in the compact mass market category going after high volume sales.

raw_title: Latin America EV Sales Report: With Over 200,000 Units Sold in Q3, EVs Now Stand at 12% Market Share!
title: Latin America EV Sales Report: With Over 200,000 Units Sold in Q3, EVs Now Stand at 12% Market Share!
raw_summary: Through 2026, EVs have gained significant momentum all over the world (safe for the US), and Latin America has been no exception. Sales grew by almost 140% in the third quarter, and clock in at a very healthy 120% growth through 2026, bringing the yearly total to more than half a million units. If this trend continues, it’s all but certain we will surpass 700,000 units by the end of the year, and perhaps even get to 800,000. Another interesting bit of trivia is that sales reached 220,000 units in the third quarter, not too far behind the USA’s 266,000. In theory, this means it should be possible for LatAm to surpass total US EV sales as early as Q1 2027 … though, I would be much happier if the USA’s market starts growing strongly again and thus Latin America cannot get ahead.
summary: Through 2026, EVs have gained significant momentum all over the world (safe for the US), and Latin America has been no exception. Sales grew by almost 140% in the third quarter, and clock in at a very healthy 120% growth through 2026, bringing the yearly total to more than half a million units.
article_paragraphs: Through 2026, EVs have gained significant momentum all over the world (safe for the US), and Latin America has been no exception. Sales grew by almost 140% in the third quarter, and clock in at a very healthy 120% growth through 2026, bringing the yearly total to more than half a million units. If this trend continues, it’s all but certain we will surpass 700,000 units by the end of the year, and perhaps even get to 800,000.

Another interesting bit of trivia is that sales reached 220,000 units in the third quarter, not too far behind the USA’s 266,000. In theory, this means it should be possible for LatAm to surpass total US EV sales as early as Q1 2027 … though, I would be much happier if the USA’s market starts growing strongly again and thus Latin America cannot get ahead.

Now, to be fair, the US is much more BEV-heavy (242,000 units sold, vs 127,000 in LatAm), whereas Latin America prefers PHEVs to a higher degree (93,000 units sold vs 44,000 in the US), but, still, these are impressive results for a region overall much poorer than the US, and with a vehicle market around a third of the size. For over a decade, it was the richest countries in the world that led EV adoption, but — as many of us predicted on this very site — that has now changed.

As mentioned earlier, total EV sales reached 220,000 units, surpassing for the first time the 200,000 mark and growing a healthy 140% YoY, and a strong 17% from Q2. BEVs grew faster than PHEVs (146% vs 130%), and thus now represent 57.5% of all EV sales in the region, slightly below the 58% result for Q2.
Market share grew to 12%, up from 10.7% in Q2 and 5.5% in Q3 last year, a pretty strong result. This brought market share above 10% through 2026, 5.9% BEV and 4.3% PHEV.

Latin America’s overall vehicle market is growing at rates of around 10% annually, but thanks to strong EV growth, combustion-based powertrains (HEV, MHEV and ICEV) are stagnant: they fell by 3.7% last quarter, and barely grew by 3.1% this one, meaning it’s very likely that we’re reaching “Peak Combustion” in Latin America and the market will only go down from 2027 onwards.

Sales wise, we have a pretty stable list, with Brazil being the unsurprising winner, followed by Mexico and Colombia, just as in Q2. Uruguay follows, but then we have a new rising star: Ecuador, which nearly reached 5,000 BEVs sold last quarter! Costa Rica, Chile, and Argentina close the top 8 and make up all the countries with over 1.000 quarterly BEV sales.
PHEV sales are much more varied, though. Brazil, of course, leads again, but following come Mexico and Argentina, with Colombia in 4 th place and Ecuador in 5 th .

title: Elon Musk Threw Away $474 Million (Or More) … But May Benefit From Failing
raw_summary: Some people think Elon Musk has lost his mind. Others think he’s always been a charlatan and has just had an insane amount of luck. Some people think he’s a genius and that everything he touches will turn to gold. And then there’s also a decent portion of folks who think he’s an absolute idiot about some things but brilliant — or at least very clever — when it comes to others. Whatever you think of Elon Musk, though, there’s no denying he just threw away about half a billion dollars. Musk reportedly spent at least $474 million on the midterm elections (because one individual is allowed to do that, apparently), and yet his picks — the key people he supported — got completely crushed. The politicians he spent all of that money to get elected did not get elected, and were actually not even close to getting elected. Apparently, voters in their jurisdictions thought they were horrible choices, sometimes historically so. Imagine if all of that money he spent had been spent on something good and useful instead! (Perhaps saving the lives of starving, poverty-stricken children and babies around the world? Perhaps stopping the spread of horrible diseases, since the US government has dropped such efforts on several threats? Perhaps to provide subsidies for electric vehicles, like Tesla sells, since Republicans in Congress and Donald Trump killed those? Perhaps to use solar power instead of fossil fuels to power AI data centers?)

Whatever you think of Elon Musk, though, there’s no denying he just threw away about half a billion dollars.

Musk reportedly spent at least $474 million on the midterm elections (because one individual is allowed to do that, apparently), and yet his picks — the key people he supported — got completely crushed. The politicians he spent all of that money to get elected did not get elected, and were actually not even close to getting elected. Apparently, voters in their jurisdictions thought they were horrible choices, sometimes historically so. Imagine if all of that money he spent had been spent on something good and useful instead! (Perhaps saving the lives of starving, poverty-stricken children and babies around the world? Perhaps stopping the spread of horrible diseases, since the US government has dropped such efforts on several threats? Perhaps to provide subsidies for electric vehicles, like Tesla sells, since Republicans in Congress and Donald Trump killed those? Perhaps to use solar power instead of fossil fuels to power AI data centers?)
Why did Elon Musk spend a whopping half a billion dollars (or more) on the 2026 midterm elections?
I know there are some people who don’t see this, but it’s been clear for a while that the following things are true about Elon Musk:

Musk largely targeted Texas with his political spending, and Texas had an epic, historic blue wave. Something that has been dreamt about for decades came true in dramatic fashion despite Elon Musk spending hundreds of millions of dollars to try to stop it. Ironically, Democratic politicians are the ones who support electric vehicles and solar power, key segments of Musk’s empire. It was California, led by Democrats, that birthed Tesla Motors and enabled it to grow and develop into an industrial behemoth. It was US policies under Democratic presidents and Congresses that also provided critical help for years upon years. So, despite Elon Musk’s worst instincts and biggest efforts politically, will his businesses actually do better under the newly elected Democratic leadership? Perhaps there are some corporate issues that need reigned in or need better regulation, and perhaps people Musk brazenly and often quite rudely campaigned against will squeeze down extra hard on his corporate actions, but policymakers who support cleantech over fossil fuels should, overall, mean more good news than bad news for Tesla and its broader mission, right?

Sure, Musk threw away $474 million and lost bigly, but is he going to be better off from failing in his efforts to pick the people running his current home state and representing it in the US government? What are the actual risks he and his companies face from the people he heavily campaigned against winning their elections? What are the benefits he and Tesla will get from fossil-loving, pollution-peddling Republican politicians no longer running the show in Texas and in Congress? One has to wonder.

By the way, one of the key people Musk campaigned against, James Talarico, has a message specifically for him. “Texas is not for sale,” Talarico said. Musk spent at least $150 million to try to get Talarico’s opponent elected. “The people of Texas delivered a crystal-clear message to the world’s first trillionaire: Texas is not for sale,” Talarico added. “The power in this state, in this country, belongs to the people, and we’ve got to make sure it stays that way.” What do the people want? Well, the people want clean air, clean and cheap energy, and less money in politics. Shouldn’t all of those things help Musk? On that last one, after all, if he wasn’t allowed to pour so much money into politics, he wouldn’t have thrown away half a billion dollars.

Some people think he’s a genius and that everything he touches will turn to gold.

raw_title: Who Controls the Battery in Your Driveway?
title: Who Controls the Battery in Your Driveway?
raw_summary: Tesla brought home power backup to America. In Australia, an update is switching it off. North American owners just got Powershare with Powerwall. Australian owners of existing Teslas got a software update that appears to block the third-party gear they use to power their homes. It is a test case for who really controls the battery in your driveway. Mark Purcell is an electrical engineer and energy advocate based in Noosa Heads, Queensland, Australia. He owns two Teslas and a bidirectional DC charger, and has been a member of the Australian Electric Vehicle Association since 2022. He has contributed content to CleanTechnica previously .
summary: Tesla brought home power backup to America. In Australia, an update is switching it off. North American owners just got Powershare with Powerwall. Australian owners of existing Teslas got a software update that appears to block the third-party gear they use to power their homes.
article_paragraphs: Tesla brought home power backup to America. In Australia, an update is switching it off. North American owners just got Powershare with Powerwall. Australian owners of existing Teslas got a software update that appears to block the third-party gear they use to power their homes. It is a test case for who really controls the battery in your driveway.

Mark Purcell is an electrical engineer and energy advocate based in Noosa Heads, Queensland, Australia. He owns two Teslas and a bidirectional DC charger, and has been a member of the Australian Electric Vehicle Association since 2022. He has contributed content to CleanTechnica previously .

On 12 October, my Model Y ran my house. Through a Sigenergy bidirectional DC charger in my garage on Australia’s Sunshine Coast, it supplied about 25 kW to my home. The battery in my driveway holds several times the energy of a typical home battery, and I have already paid for it.

That may not last. Owners in several countries report that Tesla software from the 2026.38 branch, rolling out since October, cuts third-party discharge within minutes. On the Tesla Motors Club forum, owners describe power stopping after about three minutes with a battery management alert, or after 15 to 20 minutes whatever the load. The old Camp Mode and Service Mode workarounds no longer help. Drive Tesla Canada has covered the reports. EleJoy, Tlyard and Sigenergy users are all affected, and Tlyard now warns customers that Tesla’s 2026 software detects “simulated charging” and may cut the power link.
The release notes ? “Security improvements” and minor fixes. Nothing about switching off a function owners use every day.

Here is the part that should interest readers everywhere. The same 2026.38 branch delivered Powershare with Powerwall home backup to owners in the US and Canada. That is a good thing. Tesla has finally joined Ford, GM, and Kia in letting the car back up the house.

Australia did not get it. Tesla Australia has said Powershare cannot be retrofitted to existing vehicles, and here Powershare is vehicle-to-load only. So, for every existing Tesla on Australian roads, third-party equipment is the only way to put the car to work for the home. If the software now blocks that equipment, Australian owners are left with nothing: not Tesla’s solution, and not anyone else’s.

The Tesla Australia owner’s manual says: “Do not use the Battery as a stationary power source. Doing so voids the warranty.” Tesla’s own Australian warranty page is narrower. It excludes damage caused by third-party adaptors or chargers, not the whole warranty.

article_paragraphs: Health advocates, environmental groups, heat pump installers, local electeds celebrate decision as.

SAN FRANCISCO — The Bay Area Air District voted today to move forward with the strongest clean appliance standards in the nation, putting millions of Bay Area homes on a path to switch from gas water heaters to zero-emission alternatives. Beginning in 2028, households will be required to install water heater appliances that meet clean air standards as old gas units burn out, with exemptions approved today for low-income households and complicated installations.

Gas appliances in Bay Area homes and buildings generate more smog-forming nitrogen oxide pollution than all of the region’s passenger cars combined. The Air District estimates its clean appliance standards for water heaters and furnaces could prevent up to 85 premature deaths and 15,000 asthma attacks each year.

The switch also saves families money. New research from RMI finds $360 in annual savings for Bay Area residents from switching from gas water heater to a heat pump. Analysis from SPUR projects $315 million in rebates for home energy efficiency will be available in the next three years to support the transition.
The vote follows thousands of public comments in support of the standards, despite an industry-backed opposition campaign linked to oil interests .

“The research makes it clear that climate policies and affordability go hand-in-hand and today the Bay Area is taking the historic step of making clean home appliances the standard for a better future,” said Melissa Yu, Campaign Strategist for Clean Heat, Sierra Club . “A transition toward zero-emission gas heaters will reduce a key source of smog pollution, launch programs to help get more people access better technological solutions and lower energy costs. Today’s vote is a victory for cleaner air and for energy affordability.”

“Today’s vote will supercharge the job growth we’re already seeing at heat pump businesses like mine, opening new pathways for early-career Bay Area workers looking for family-sustaining wages and meaningful work. The Bay Area Air District showed real leadership in approving these standards. We’re proud to be on the front lines of equipping homes with energy-efficient technologies that cut energy bills, clean the air, and make homes more comfortable,” said Owen Krebs Grimsich, CEO and owner of 1-888 Heat Pumps.

“Today, the Bay Area chose clean air over fossil fuel pollution. Under these standards, when a household’s gas water heater wears out, it will be replaced with cleaner, more efficient technology like a heat pump, so millions of residents will breathe easier and save money on their energy bills. The Bay Area Air District showed real leadership, and the rest of the country should follow its lead,” said Tony Sirna, Deputy Policy Director for Buildings at Evergreen Action .

Following multiple test mule sightings , the teaser images show the updated model without camouflage, although dramatic lighting keeps some details concealed.
article_paragraphs: Volkswagen India has released the first official teaser of the upcoming Virtus facelift, offering a clearer look at the sedan’s exterior ahead of launch. Following multiple test mule sightings , the teaser images show the updated model without camouflage, although dramatic lighting keeps some details concealed.

The most noticeable changes are concentrated at the front. The Virtus retains its slim headlamp layout, with LED daytime running lights outlining the lighting units. A narrow upper grille connects the headlamps, with a prominent Volkswagen emblem in the centre and a red GT badge on one side.

Below this, the bumper gets a more aggressive appearance, featuring a wide lower intake with geometric detailing. The outer sections have sculpted surrounds and horizontal elements, giving the facelift a more pronounced sporting character. The redesigned bumper also appears to do away with separate front fog lamps , with horizontal inserts occupying the outer sections instead.

Earlier reports had suggested a connected LED light strip and an illuminated Volkswagen logo. Much to the relief of fans who prefer a cleaner front-end design, the Virtus facelift skips the connected LED DRL trend. The teaser confirms separate daytime running lights within the headlamps, with a conventional grille linking the two sides.

The blue exterior finish is another highlight, contrasting with the dark alloy wheels and black mirror housings. Close-up shots reveal an angular alloy wheel design, while the familiar shoulder line, conventional door handles and sloping roofline continue.

A GT badge on the front fender reinforces the identity of the car shown, though the complete variant lineup remains unannounced. An overhead shot also reveals a single pane sunroof and shark-fin antenna.

At the rear, the Virtus features distinctive red LED lighting elements within split tail lamp assemblies. The lamps extend onto the boot lid, while a dark horizontal section visually links the two sides. A boot-mounted lip spoiler adds to the GT’s sporty appearance. The rear bumper also features a dark lower insert with patterned detailing, and parking sensors are visible in the teaser.

The Volkswagen emblem remains centrally positioned on the boot, with GT branding towards the lower right. Together, these elements give the updated sedan a refreshed identity while retaining the familiar Virtus silhouette.

title: Retro 1970s Survivor: A 1977 Honda Z50A "Monkey Bike
raw_summary: This is an original Honda Z50A from 1977, it now benefits from significant recent restoration work, including all new paintwork, refurbished original parts, and a professionally rebuilt engine. Honda minibikes like the Z50A formed the backbone of the 1970s junior motorcycle boom, they sold in their thousands from coast to coast (and around the world), and many motorcyclists got their first taste of life on two wheels on them.
summary: This is an original Honda Z50A from 1977, it now benefits from significant recent restoration work, including all new paintwork, refurbished original parts, and a professionally rebuilt engine. Honda minibikes like the Z50A formed the backbone of the 1970s junior motorcycle boom, they sold in their thousands from coast to coast (and around the world), and many motorcyclists got their first taste of life on two wheels on them.
article_paragraphs: This is an original Honda Z50A from 1977, it now benefits from significant recent restoration work, including all new paintwork, refurbished original parts, and a professionally rebuilt engine.

Honda minibikes like the Z50A formed the backbone of the 1970s junior motorcycle boom, they sold in their thousands from coast to coast (and around the world), and many motorcyclists got their first taste of life on two wheels on them.

The Honda Z50A Mini Trail had actually started life as a fairground ride in Japan, long before it became a two-wheeled zeitgeist of life in 1970s America. In October of 1961, Honda opened two motoring-themed amusement parks, Tama Tech in the Tokyo suburbs and Ikoma Tech in Nara Prefecture, and built a miniature motorcycle called the Z100 for visitors to ride.
The Honda Z50A Mini Trail had actually started life as a fairground ride in Japan, long before it became a two-wheeled zeitgeist of life in 1970s America. Image courtesy of Honda.

The little Z100 sat on 5-inch tires and used the Super Cub’s 49cc overhead-valve single, a 3-speed gearbox and an automatic centrifugal clutch. Honda had no plans to sell it, they just wanted a fun and easy fairground ride for people who had never thrown a leg over a motorcycle before. It was quickly nicknamed the “monkey bike” because of how adults looked when riding them (particularly when viewed from the back) with their knees up and arms out, due to the small size of the Z100.

Honda’s no-public-sales plans changed after the Z100 appeared at the Frankfurt and London Motor Shows in late 1962, where they were very warmly received by show attendees – Honda shipped 20 of them to its European operation that December for evaluation.

Long story short, the Europeans loved it, and a road-legal export model soon followed, the Honda CZ100, with a stiffer frame to carry adults and a fuel tank borrowed from the pre-existing Honda Sports Cub. Production began in 1964 on a small assembly line in a corner of the Suzuka factory, where five workers built 20 bikes a day. Around 2,500 were made in three years, exported mainly to France and Germany.

The first of these monkey bikes that sold in Japan was the 1967 Honda Z50M. It switched to the Super Cub’s overhead-cam engine, added lights for the road, and had a seat and handlebars that folded so the bike could ride in a car trunk. Honda didn’t yet build a car with a trunk big enough to take one, but that arrived two years later with the introduction of the Honda 1300 in 1969.

raw_title: Locally-Made Mercedes-Benz Electric GLC Launched At Rs. 78.50 Lakh
title: Locally-Made Mercedes-Benz Electric GLC Launched At Rs. 78.50 Lakh
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - The GLC 400 4Matic Electric becomes the first locally built Mercedes-Benz based on the MB.EA-M platform as Pune joins Bremen in its global production network Mercedes-Benz India has started local production of the all-new Electric GLC at its Chakan facility in Pune, Maharashtra. The first locally assembled unit is the GLC 400 4Matic Electric, which carries an ex-showroom price of Rs. 78.50 lakh across India. Deliveries are scheduled to commence in mid-November 2026, placing the electric SUV at the centre of the company’s next phase of local manufacturing. The Electric GLC brings two major technology firsts to the Indian production facility. It is the first locally manufactured Mercedes-Benz based on the MB.EA-M electric vehicle architecture and also the first locally built model to use the Mercedes-Benz Operating System, or MB.OS. The Pune facility is only the second plant globally to manufacture this generation of the Electric GLC, following the company’s factory in Bremen, Germany. The production milestone was marked in the presence of Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Sunetra Pawar and senior Mercedes-Benz Group executives, including Chairman Ola Källenius and CTO Joerg Burzer. The company says the Electric GLC is assembled on the same flexible production line used for combustion-engine vehicles. This arrangement allows the Pune plant to handle electric and petrol or diesel models on a shared manufacturing line. Mercedes-Benz India has committed an additional Rs. 200 crore investment in 2026 towards manufacturing operations, new product start up activities and digitisation. Its cumulative investment in India now stands at Rs. 3,200 crore, which the company describes as the highest among luxury carmakers in the country. Mercedes-Benz also says it has sold more than 2.4 lakh vehicles locally, another record figure for a luxury manufacturer in India. The new model also introduces the MB.OS digital platform to locally manufactured Mercedes-Benz vehicles. Dealer news sources Automotive News and Cox Automotive report that the average new car spent 82 days on the lot in October, with a 75-day target being an industry-wide benchmark. The refuge is home to a diverse array of grasslands, wetlands, and woods that attract red foxes, painted turtles, osprey, river otters, and countless other rarely seen species – and the ADA accessible path being laid down by the L25 Electric compact wheel loader will allow wheelchair-bound visitors to travel a half-mile-long trail around one of the pond . Meanwhile, the ECR25 Electric compact excavator will be digging trenches to improve drainage from the pond and helping to place a viewing platform that extends out over the water.

article_paragraphs: On Wednesday, NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory , a space telescope that's been in orbit since 2004, finally re-entered Earth's atmosphere above Indonesia. However, it appears to have done so with a risk of casualties five times beyond what NASA technical standards mandate. How and why this happened isn't immediately clear; NASA Public Affairs Specialist Alise Fisher told Jalopnik, "In the leadup to Swift's Nov. 20, 2004, launch, NASA determined the risk was consistent with mission requirements as allowed by agency policy." Somewhere between launch and reentry, that risk assessment shifted. It's unlikely that anybody made a specific mistake; this is probably the result of, well, space being hard. Still, it does highlight that our main defense against the detritus of astronomical ambitions is pure luck.

Swift is only crashing to Earth because it ran out of fuel to stay in orbit or adjust its trajectory. To NASA's credit, it did throw $30 million at a private company in an unprecedented attempt to rescue Swift with another satellite that would pull it back up into safe orbit. Sadly, the rescue satellite itself failed, dooming Swift to this fate.

In formal terms, Swift suffered an "uncontrolled reentry," which basically means it had no propulsion and just fell from space. NASA's own requirements, most recently updated in 2021 but going all the way back to 2001, state: "For uncontrolled reentry, the risk of human casualty from surviving debris shall be less than 0.0001 (1:10,000)." If you're not aware, there's no actual law requiring that satellites de-orbit in some sort of safe way that won't, you know, crash into a city or kill anyone. So our shield against the skies is just statistics. This is the threshold at which NASA feels the risk is acceptable. For reference, in all of history, just about 10,000 satellites have de-orbited , so... statistically we're due. And that was before we were putting tens of thousands of satellites up every few years .

In Swift's instance, however, NASA played its cards a little close to its chest. For one thing, it did not put out a risk assessment for the reentry , which is unusual. Then, in the middle of a longer announcement , the agency mentioned that Swift's risk of human casualties was actually "1 in 2,100." That's a risk of human injury or death five times beyond what it was meant to be.

Fortunately, the odds appear to have resolved in our favor. There are no reports of anyone being struck by space debris from Swift. Most of the satellite was expected to burn up during reentry; the trouble would come from whatever survived, likely dense pieces like the telescope lens or the reaction wheels. If any of those made it to the surface, there doesn't appear to have been a person around it.

That's a roll of the dice, though. At some point, as thousands of satellites de-orbit per year in our new megaconstellation era, laws should be passed to manage this formally. That would likely mean requiring controlled reentries, when the satellite still has a little fuel left to navigate to a safe spot out in the ocean. The other option, which companies like SpaceX have been pursuing, is to design the satellite to burn up entirely on reentry. The issue there is what effect all that vaporized metal might have on the atmosphere. Scientists don't yet know the answer, for the simple reason that there was never a reason to ask that question before. Now, the health of our planet may depend on it.

As space gets busier and busier, more and more will fall to us down here from up there. Up until now, the power of statistics has kept us safe. But eventually, a 1 in 10,000 chance is going to happen. Especially if some of those chances turn out to be riskier than intended.

raw_title: China's Buick Electra GS Is A Stylish Hybrid America Can't Have
title: China's Buick Electra GS Is A Stylish Hybrid America Can't Have
raw_summary: Buick hasn't offered a sedan in the U.S. since sales of the Regal ended in 2020. But it's a totally different story in China, where SUV haters can choose from multiple low-riding four-door cars, including the handsome, electrified Electra L7. Now, Buick's Chinese division is gearing up to launch its Electra GS little brother, and you have to wonder if America is missing out. Details of the Electra GS were revealed by China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology filings ahead of the official debut, and they tell us the production car has changed quite a bit since GM showed the Electra GS concept (below) at the Shanghai Auto Show in 2025. The LED headlights have been inverted, and the Buick badge moved from the hood to a front facia that features less body-color plastic. The concept was incredibly handsome, but maybe looked a little too much like a Tesla Model 3 around the front. The production car looks less like a Tesla, but sacrifices some eye candy points.

article_paragraphs: Buick hasn't offered a sedan in the U.S. since sales of the Regal ended in 2020. But it's a totally different story in China, where SUV haters can choose from multiple low-riding four-door cars, including the handsome, electrified Electra L7. Now, Buick's Chinese division is gearing up to launch its Electra GS little brother, and you have to wonder if America is missing out.

Details of the Electra GS were revealed by China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology filings ahead of the official debut, and they tell us the production car has changed quite a bit since GM showed the Electra GS concept (below) at the Shanghai Auto Show in 2025. The LED headlights have been inverted, and the Buick badge moved from the hood to a front facia that features less body-color plastic. The concept was incredibly handsome, but maybe looked a little too much like a Tesla Model 3 around the front. The production car looks less like a Tesla, but sacrifices some eye candy points.

An imminent ban on pop-out door handles in China meant the concept's had to go, and though the fastback profile is carried across, the show car's traditional sedan trunk has made way for a more practical hatch. The taillights are also new, and so is the "Buick" lettering spelled out at the rear of the car.

Another genuinely massive change is the productions GS's massive reduction in scale. MIIT data shows it's 196.1 inches (4,980 mm) long, but the concept (pictured above) was a huge 208.7 inches (5,300 mm). Same thing with wheelbase. The concept's axles were 126 inches (3,200 mm) apart, but the production GS wheelbase measures 112.8 inches (2,865 mm), making the finished car similar in size to a Toyota Crown , rather than a Mercedes S-Class.

The biggest switch of all, though, takes place under the hood. GM didn't reveal much in the way of technical details about the concept, but it did confirm it was a fully electric car that rode on a dedicated EV platform, giving a totally flat floor. But, like Adam West's 1966 Batman jumping on the Batpoles inside Wayne Manor dressed in a comfy cardigan, and emerging inside the Batcave in full caped crusader garb 100 ft (31 m) down, the GS bound for dealers has arrived for duty as a plug-in hybrid.

Base cars pair a 97 horsepower (98 PS) naturally aspirated 1.5-liter inline-4 with a 221 hp (224 PS) electric motor, but a more expensive variant swaps the NA gas motor for a turbocharged version of the same, making 154 hp (156 PS). We'll have wait for the full China debut to find out more about the GS, including whether the interior looks anything like the concept's (below). But don't pin your hopes on seeing that yoke steering wheel — we can already see a conventional steering wheel is present in the studio images of the exterior.

Back in the U.S., GM's sales have been hurt by its lack of hybrid offerings. The automaker was so sure EVs would dominate the car market by the end of the decade that it didn't bother developing them, except for the Corvette E-Ray (now renamed Grand Sport X). Rival brands like Toyota and Hyundai hedged their bets, and made both, and are now reaping the rewards, while GM is rushing to catch up toward the end of the decade.

Could the GS work here? Absolutely, but it's not likely. GM does import vehicles from China, including Chinese-built Buick Envision from China , although production of that model is due to shift to Kansas in 2028. Complicating matters is the fact that the GS is the result of a joint venture between GM and China's SAIC, and new restrictions on Chinese software that take effect with the 2027 model year would make it tricky to get this car compliant for the U.S. market, even if production was shifted to North America to avoid tariffs. Overall, we'd say don't hold your breath for this Buick.

title: Urgent Safety Alert: GM is recalling more than 67,000 Cadillac and Chevy EVs over a brake software defect
raw_summary: General Motors (GM) issued a recall affecting more than 67,000 Cadillac and Chevy EVs because a software glitch can cause a temporary loss of braking. The recall comes after a 2024 Cadillac Lyriq ran into a garage (at a low speed). On April 10, 2026, a GM tech expert submitted a report to GM’s Speak Up for Safety (SUFS) program for review.

article_paragraphs: General Motors (GM) issued a recall affecting more than 67,000 Cadillac and Chevy EVs because a software glitch can cause a temporary loss of braking.
The recall comes after a 2024 Cadillac Lyriq ran into a garage (at a low speed). On April 10, 2026, a GM tech expert submitted a report to GM’s Speak Up for Safety (SUFS) program for review.

After internal testing, GM was able to replicate the glitch, similar to a recall it issued in 2024. GM said the issue stems from a software glitch with the brake system control module (BSCM) that can cause a temporary loss of braking while driving under certain conditions.
When drivers lightly tap the brakes during a sharp turn and the vehicle hits a bump, the software’s slip calculation may misinterpret wheel movement.
In some instances, it can lead to a temporary loss of braking. The glitch only affects pAWD vehicles, including certain Cadillac Lyriq, Celestiq, Vistiq, and Chevy Blazer EV.

raw_title: Almost no one uses AI agents to book their Uber, company says
title: Almost no one uses AI agents to book their Uber, company says
raw_summary: Very few people are using personal AI agents to order Ubers, apparently. On the transportation giant’s third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday, the company said that only four rides were ordered through an AI agent during its busiest week in October: the week of Halloween. While more people used an AI agent to order food through its delivery service, Uber Eats, the volume was still fairly small compared to the overall number of trips.
