article_paragraphs: Very few people are using personal AI agents to order Ubers, apparently. On the transportation giant’s third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday, the company said that only four rides were ordered through an AI agent during its busiest week in October: the week of Halloween.
While more people used an AI agent to order food through its delivery service, Uber Eats, the volume was still fairly small compared to the overall number of trips.

Uber’s chief financial officer, Balaji Krishnamurthy, told Wall Street analysts on the call that the company handled around 320 million trips and orders across Uber and Uber Eats during the week of Halloween, but only 500 Uber Eats orders were placed by an AI agent.

“It is very, very early and very limited traction that we are seeing so far,” said CEO Dara Khosrowshahi, referring to the low number of orders placed by AI agents. “Listen, we hope that there will be more traction.”

The surprisingly low numbers of AI-initiated transactions come amid growing hype for a new wave of AI agents that don’t just answer questions but also handle tasks on users’ behalf. There’s been an explosion of personal AI startups, including one of the buzziest, Instinct, which was founded last year and raised its most recent round of funding at a $10 billion valuation. Meta’s Muse also became the No. 1 app in Apple’s U.S. App Store last month, topping 10 million users, per Meta’s own reporting . The company said many were using it to shop and transact with businesses.
OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and SpaceXAI (Grok) are also now offering their own AI agents, as are numerous smaller startups.

Still, early numbers from public companies indicate the agentic web still has a long way to go. DoorDash, for instance, said last week on its earnings call that it has only received a few hundred orders from AI agents so far, as most customers are still placing orders through the DoorDash app.

Uber is seeing the same behavior, it seems. Khosrowshahi pointed out that the average time to book a ride is only 50 seconds in the company’s app, and re-ordering a favorite food only takes 90 seconds. That suggests an AI agent isn’t necessarily saving anyone time.

title: Mercedes' Smart Rear Window Delivers Passive Aggressive Messages To The People Behind You
raw_summary: Americans have been sending messages to the drivers behind them ever since Forest P. Gill turned a load of self-adhesive paper into the first bumper sticker in 1946. But now Mercedes wants to give the bumper sticker a digital update by allowing you to turn your rear window into a pixelated message board. Mini LEDs embedded in the rear window light up when needed to create the messages, and they are invisible the rest of the time so as not to spoil the driver's view of what's going on behind him. This being Mercedes, the messages are not in the realm of "Why don't you act like your hairline and take a few steps back" or "My other car is a Mercedes." They're sensible, safety-focused, and hilariously passive aggressive.

But now Mercedes wants to give the bumper sticker a digital update by allowing you to turn your rear window into a pixelated message board.
article_paragraphs: Americans have been sending messages to the drivers behind them ever since Forest P. Gill turned a load of self-adhesive paper into the first bumper sticker in 1946. But now Mercedes wants to give the bumper sticker a digital update by allowing you to turn your rear window into a pixelated message board.

Mini LEDs embedded in the rear window light up when needed to create the messages, and they are invisible the rest of the time so as not to spoil the driver's view of what's going on behind him. This being Mercedes, the messages are not in the realm of "Why don't you act like your hairline and take a few steps back" or "My other car is a Mercedes." They're sensible, safety-focused, and hilariously passive aggressive.

Someone blasting you from behind with their high beams? Show them the headlight symbol with a massive red line through it. Tailgater trouble ? The "keep distance" message kindly suggests that back off a little. Other worthy possibilities include warnings of a pedestrian crossing or a crash ahead, or a signal that the car in front of them is about to back into a parking bay.

These are the officially sanctioned messages. Mercedes makes no mention of drivers being allowed to come up with their own, and probably for good reason. But you just know that it'll take about five minutes after this tech hits the streets for some enterprising coder to hack the system and deliver digital abuse to any following BMW, Audi or Lexus.

Mercedes' engineers haven't only been working out how to display messages on the rear window. They've been busy with the side windows and windshield, too, though the LEDs involved are understandably much smaller. We've had head-up displays for over 20 years, but instead of limiting displays to a small area in front of the driver, Mercedes wants to turn a large area of windshield into a giant communication surface. A projector in the top of the dashboard beams content upwards, and a transparent film laminated into the glass reflects the projected wavelengths using "holographic optical elements" (HOE). Hyundai showed something similar last year.

The light is bundled in such a way that the image can be seen in all conditions, including bright sunlight. But the clever part is that anything projected onto the passenger side of the glass can't be viewed by the driver, and vice versa. Which means passengers can watch videos and movies while the car is in motion. Whether they will, is another matter. Automakers have been pushing expensive passenger-side digital dashboard screens for the past few years, which you'd think would give a better viewing experience than this new projected tech, but one study found that they're rarely used .

Mercedes says other uses beyond entertainment include video calls and displaying points of interest along your route. That's likely to become a big deal in the years to come as businesses like restaurants, hotels and tourist attractions pay to appear as stop-off suggestions in cars from all brands . No timeframe was given for the tech's introduction, but if Mercedes is showing it, it must have production intent. Our guess is you'll be able to digitally tut-tut at the driver behind you before the end of the decade.

raw_title: Nabrawind’s Crane-Free Wind Towers Face a Supplier Test
title: Nabrawind's Crane-Free Wind Towers Face a Supplier Test
raw_summary: Spain’s Nabrawind has developed a way to install exceptionally tall wind turbine towers without bringing an enormous crawler crane to the site. Its Nabralift system uses a tubular upper tower supported by a three-legged steel structure. Hydraulic equipment raises the assembled turbine while modular sections are inserted below it near ground level. The lifting frame can then be removed and used on another installation. This addresses genuine logistical and construction problems, particularly at remote sites where specialist cranes are expensive to transport and where wind can interrupt conventional lifting operations. The company has progressed beyond demonstration-scale hardware. In September 2026, UL Solutions issued type certification for Envision’s 7.8 MW turbine on Nabrawind’s 188-meter tower. Fortescue is using 17 of those tower configurations at the 133 MW Nullagine wind project in Western Australia’s Pilbara region, where construction is underway. Nabrawind previously erected a 160-meter prototype in Spain in under two weeks and has supplied smaller commercial towers in Morocco and France.

The company has progressed beyond demonstration-scale hardware. In September 2026, UL Solutions issued type certification for Envision’s 7.8 MW turbine on Nabrawind’s 188-meter tower. Fortescue is using 17 of those tower configurations at the 133 MW Nullagine wind project in Western Australia’s Pilbara region, where construction is underway. Nabrawind previously erected a 160-meter prototype in Spain in under two weeks and has supplied smaller commercial towers in Morocco and France.

The engineering benefits are credible. Nabrawind reports using roughly 20% less tower steel than comparable conventional tubular designs and reducing foundation concrete by as much as 80%, depending on the design and site. Those are supplier claims rather than independently established savings across all wind farms. The potential to avoid large cranes, simplify transport and raise turbines in windier conditions could also matter substantially to total installed cost and construction schedules. High hub heights only earn their keep when those costs are justified by the electricity generated over the project’s life.

The current deployment has an unusual commercial structure. Fortescue acquired Nabrawind in September 2025 and is building Nullagine to serve its own mining operations. Fortescue has the capital, internal electricity demand and industrial incentive to support a technology it owns. Successful installation in that context would be important evidence of construction performance, but it would not establish that an unrelated wind developer can finance and maintain the same system under ordinary third-party commercial arrangements.

Nabralift’s proprietary construction approach creates a procurement issue. Conventional tubular towers can be sourced from several qualified manufacturers, and experienced contractors can compete for much of their construction work. A developer selecting Nabralift currently depends on one supplier for the core tower system, specialist lifting knowledge and associated support. Wind turbine original-equipment manufacturers also create supplier dependencies, but concentrating another critical part of the project in a proprietary installation system requires its own contract and risk assessment.

A type certificate provides valuable technical assurance about the certified turbine-and-tower configuration. A lender or insurer still needs enforceable delivery schedules, long-term warranties, repair and maintenance provisions, clarity on replacement parts, and a workable remedy if the supplier’s capacity or commercial priorities change. These questions become more important when a wind farm must operate for 25 years or longer and there is no qualified alternative provider of the same system.

Nabrawind’s next important proof point is an independently developed and financed large wind farm that accepts those risks on commercial terms. Qualified installation partners, credible long-term service arrangements and greater competitive capacity could make its engineering advantages easier for developers to buy. The 188-meter tower has earned technical attention; its broader market depends on financing and procurement confidence catching up with the machinery.

My full TFIE Strategy Briefing assessment examines Nabrawind’s self-erecting design, Fortescue’s Nullagine deployment and the supplier concentration that independent wind developers would have to manage. It follows my earlier assessment of 300-meter wind towers , where construction economics were the central challenge.

raw_title: Rimac Is Helping BMW Create Two New Mystery Models
title: Rimac Is Helping BMW Create Two New Mystery Models
raw_summary: Rimac has transformed from a small Croatian brand that built just eight examples of the wild Concept One into a technology and manufacturing juggernaut that now owns Bugatti. When it's not building hypercars, Rimac supplies electric drivetrains to some of the industry's top automotive brands, and boss Mate Rimac has confirmed it's working on two more cars with BMW. The new i7 is the first model from BMW to use a jointly developed battery system created alongside Rimac. This system combines the German automaker's Gen6 4695 lithium-ion cylindrical cells with its Gen5 module-based technology into a scalable architecture that other vehicles can use. Rimac manufactures the battery system at its campus near Zagreb. In a recent interview with Auto News , Mate Rimac confirmed that "there are two more cars in the pipeline" being developed alongside BMW. Details about these new models haven't been announced, so we can only speculate. New products from BMW's Neue Klasse line-up seem most likely.

In the same interview, Rimac shared how it landed an important supply contract with BMW. He gave BMW executives a tour of the Rimac Campus while it was still in the early stages of construction, and pointed out where he planned to establish a production line for BMW at the site. The German automaker said it had no contracts with Rimac.

"It doesn't matter," Mate Rimac replied, "I'm building it for you," reassuring the German brand that Rimac was committed to the project. "BMW is premium," he added. "You have to be the best technically and commercially to supply them. They have to be competitive on the market and they cannot pay a premium to get components from a company that's not optimized. To win that business, we had to be better than everyone on the market both technically and commercially."

A wide range of cars feature Rimac technology. These include the Koenigsegg Regera, Aston Martin Valkyrie, Porsche 911 GTS T-Hybrid, and the new Ceer EVs from Saudi Arabia . In September, a consortium of investors purchased Porsche's 21% shareholding in Rimac Group and its 45% stake in the Bugatti Rimac joint venture. Free from Porsche's influence, Rimac says it can now make decisions faster. "A big company like Porsche is always risk aware and risk averse, and the decision-making process is long", Mate Rimac said. "Now I can sit down with my management team, make a decision and go. Something that would have taken six months to decide waiting for board approvals gets done much quicker."

raw_title: Mercedes Delays U.S. GLC Production, Leaving the Model Vulnerable to Tariffs
title: Mercedes Delays U.S. GLC Production, Leaving the Model Vulnerable to Tariffs
raw_summary: Mercedes-Benz is delaying the start of its U.S. production of the GLC-class crossover, according to Automotive News . The automaker had originally planned for production of the GLC to begin in late 2027, but the paper reports that it has now been delayed to 2030. When the U.S. production does begin, it will take place at the automaker’s Vance, Alabama, plant. According to the AN report, Mercedes is delaying the move in production to wait for the arrival of the next-generation GLC-class. “Investing in the plant for about half a life cycle and then having to retool for the next-generation GLC doesn’t make a lot of sense financially,” Sam Fiorani, the vice president of AutoForecast, told the outlet. The Alabama plant, in its current configuration, is home to the GLS-class and GLE-class SUVs, along with their electric counterparts.

After announcing the name of its new midsize electric pickup this summer, Ford said the Fathom will start at just $28,350 for the standard-range model.

article_paragraphs: Ford’s upcoming Fathom electric pickup will be among the most affordable EVs in the US, starting at $28,350. Even pricier trims will start at under $40,000.
After announcing the name of its new midsize electric pickup this summer, Ford said the Fathom will start at just $28,350 for the standard-range model.

Even with the $1,595 delivery fee, prices will start at under $30,000. On the company’s third-quarter earnings call last week, CEO Jim Farley said the Fathom, Ford’s first vehicle off the Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform, remains on track to launch in Q4 2027.
Last Tuesday, a day before earnings, Farley said he had the chance to test-drive a prototype and that it “completely blew me away.”
The 0 to 60 mph, huge room inside, and the hands-free, ADAS experience was like “something I’ve never experienced,” Farley told investors.
Ford’s CEO added that the Fathom is a “breakthrough product” that’s highly capable and affordable. The MSRP under $30,000 and low cost of ownership, Farley said, is perfect for today’s market.

The electric pickup will use a zonal electrical architecture and a 48-volt system to cut costs. It will also offer bidirectional charging, enabling it to power your home to save on energy costs or during an outage.
When asked how the company plans to upsell the Fathom beyond the $28,350 starting price, Andrew Frick, president of Ford Model e, offered some insight.

article_paragraphs: Police in L.A. aren't messing around anymore when it comes to street takeovers

Last week, we told you how deputies in Los Angeles County managed to shut down a couple of street takeovers before they started . This week, we're learning that the task force there appears eager to make sure that wasn't a one-hit wonder. Authorities say a group traveled from Northern California for more illegal events over the weekend. Seven cars now have a month-long stay at the impound lot.

According to the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, the gatherings went by "Bay to LA." Its Street Takeover Task Force conducted several enforcement operations, making 22 arrests and issuing 74 citations. Another 22 vehicles received citations requiring state referee inspections. As we've also noted in the past, those inspections can completely shift the way a person approaches the future of their car use. The LASD didn't provide a list of what cars were impounded, but it did post a video to social media , which gives us a good indication. Included in the video are an SN95 Ford Mustang convertible, a similarly aged Chevrolet Camaro, a Pontiac G8, at least one Chevy SS, and a third-gen Lexus LS.

The alleged offenses included reckless driving , exhibition of speed, driving with a suspended license, felony evading, felony illegal firearms possession, and felony conspiracy to commit reckless driving. Deputies worked in Carson, Cerritos, Compton, Lynwood, Commerce, Lakewood, and unincorporated parts of the county.

Interestingly, there's a couple of patterns emerging here. Yes, last week, police cracked down on two takeovers, but how they did so is key. Authorities specifically credited their ability to see these events advertised on social media for helping them do their job. During that operation, police arrested another 22 people, issued 104 citations, and handed out 55 emission or exhaust violations.

This time around, it seems like the organizers once again posted about the event online before showing up. Will they keep doing that? If so, it appears as though police will be paying attention and ready to show up and shut things down.

Officers in California don't just treat drivers as participants. Occupants of the vehicle in question can end up with charges too if that vehicle is participating in the takeover. In fact, the law goes even further. Police can cite those who use their own vehicles to block an intersection even if they're not doing donuts or anything of the sort. Then, there are the spectators who can also end up with citations. That's right, just being at the scene can result in significant financial penalties.

The Temerario might be the runt of the Lamborghini supercar litter, but it's still one raging bull. Taking the reins from its widely lauded Huracan predecessor, the Temerario is the least expensive way into Lambo's supercar lineup, but it doesn’t sacrifice much performance compared to the company's Revuelto flagship—in fact, it beats its brawnier older brother to 60 mph by a tenth of a second.

Under the Temerario's origami-folded sheetmetal lies a newly developed 4.0-liter twin-turbo V-8 nestled into the car's aluminum spaceframe just ahead of the rear axle. As if 789 horsepower from the engine alone wasn’t enough, a trio of electric motors—one mounted between the engine and transmission and one at each front wheel—ups its total output to 907 Italian stallions. If you somehow tire of the sound of the flat-plane-crank V-8's goosebump-raising 10,000-rpm wail, the electric motors also allow for short periods of silent, all-electric driving. With its mighty hybrid-assisted thrust, poster-worthy looks, and agile moves, the Temerario is every inch a purebred Lambo and well worthy of supercar status.
Expert Tip: If you'd rather have a horse instead of a bull in your garage, the Ferrari 296GTB is a steed with the need for speed, and moves to match the Lambo for a similar price.
Compare the 2027 Lamborghini Temerario with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.
Lamborghini's newest bull debuted in 2026 and charges into 2027 without any notable changes.

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

The Temerario's powertrain consists of a twin-turbo 4.0-liter V-8 with a flat-plane crankshaft, a trio of axial-flux electric motors, and an eight-speed dual-clutch transmission. The Temerario's V-8 alone is good for 789 horsepower; adding the output of the three electric motors brings the total combined output to 907 horsepower. That's just 94 ponies shy of the Lamborghini Revuelto , the brand's V-12 halo car. On the Temerario, one electric motor mounts to the V-8 in front of the transmission, while the remaining two live up front, one at each wheel. The Temerario's V-8 redlines at 10,000 rpm, and the engine's peak torque of 538 pound-feet is available from 4000 to 7000 rpm. While the flat-plane-crank V-8 sounds glorious when pushed to its limit, we wish that its exhaust packed a bit more fury earlier in the rev range.

title: This Kia EV4 GT Is Made Of Actual Tennis Court Clay
raw_summary: Only a few athletes have captivated fans as much as Rafael Nadal. The retired Spanish tennis player, who spent 209 weeks as the world's number 1, has received a special present from Kia, celebrating his illustrious career. Believe it or not, the pictured full-size model of the Kia EV4 GT is made with earth gathered from the actual courts where Nadal gained the nickname "King of Clay". Though he retired from professional tennis in late 2024, Nadal has been a Kia global brand ambassador since 2006, after he won his first Grand Slam. In order to honor their longtime collaboration, Kia created a special sculpture by blending traditional styling clay with tennis court clay from Monte Carlo, Paris, Rome, and Madrid.

article_paragraphs: Only a few athletes have captivated fans as much as Rafael Nadal. The retired Spanish tennis player, who spent 209 weeks as the world's number 1, has received a special present from Kia, celebrating his illustrious career. Believe it or not, the pictured full-size model of the Kia EV4 GT is made with earth gathered from the actual courts where Nadal gained the nickname "King of Clay".

Though he retired from professional tennis in late 2024, Nadal has been a Kia global brand ambassador since 2006, after he won his first Grand Slam. In order to honor their longtime collaboration, Kia created a special sculpture by blending traditional styling clay with tennis court clay from Monte Carlo, Paris, Rome, and Madrid.

To break up the monotony of the orange material, Kia used white design tape to highlight the character lines of the EV4 GT. These accents double as a reference to the white tennis court lines and are joined by custom exterior graphics highlighting Nadal's major career milestones.

A walk around the sculpture will remind Nadal of his clay-related achievements. At the front, Kia printed "63 TITLES ON CLAY" next to the headlight and "81 CONSECUTIVE WINS ON CLAY" on the hood. The profile carries a note about the "4 FRENCH OPEN TITLES" at Roland-Garros out of Nadal's 22 Grand Slam single titles. Finally, the rear end has his signature next to "5 SEASONS AT NUMBER 1" lettering.

The unique Kia EV4 was presented to the tennis legend at his Rafa Nadal Academy in Mallorca, Spain. It has the same footprint as the production EV4 GT hatchback, but is non-drivable and doesn't have an interior. Still, it rides on production wheels and tires, so it likely rolls. Most clay models sit on special platforms with cart wheels, making it easier to move them around in tight spaces.

While Kia could have chosen a higher-end model, like the electric Stinger successor, over a compact electric hatchback for the tribute, the eye-catching material and tennis references will certainly make it a great conversation starter in Nadal's garage. After all, the "King of Clay" should have a car made of clay in his collection.

"For more than twenty years, Kia has been by my side throughout my career, through all the highs and the challenges," said Nadal . "Receiving this tribute, created from the material that has defined so much of my journey, is incredibly meaningful. It is a special reminder of everything we have shared, and I am honored by this gesture."

The automaker noted that despite the increasing use of digital tools in automotive design , clay modeling remains an integral part of vehicle development as it allows designers to judge "proportions, surfaces, finishes, and tensions" on a physical product.

raw_title: Tesla Allegedly Misled Thousands Of South Korean Customers About 'Full Self-Driving'
title: Tesla Allegedly Misled Thousands Of South Korean Customers About 'Full Self-Driving
raw_summary: Usually, when we tell you that Tesla has gotten into hot water for misleading folks about its "Full Self-Driving" Level 2 driver assistance system , it has to do with Tesla overstating just how capable of a system it is. That's not the case in South Korea, though, where the Texas-based automaker has allegedly vastly overstated the legality of FSD usage and charged customers for it nonetheless. Now, tens of thousands of Korean Tesla owners are looking for answers. Tesla apparently markets FSD in South Korea despite the fact that it knows the majority of its cars can't legally use the program in the country, the complaint from an advocacy group alleges. That means it can't be activated on the car. Soon, the complaint will be filed with the Korean Fair Trade Commission, a consumer protection agency, according to Reuters . Tesla will have to answer for why it marketed FSD to prospective buyers for years, even collecting the $6,726 lump-sum payment required for activation, even though it couldn't legally be used.

That's not the case in South Korea, though, where the Texas-based automaker has allegedly vastly overstated the legality of FSD usage and charged customers for it nonetheless.
article_paragraphs: Usually, when we tell you that Tesla has gotten into hot water for misleading folks about its "Full Self-Driving" Level 2 driver assistance system , it has to do with Tesla overstating just how capable of a system it is. That's not the case in South Korea, though, where the Texas-based automaker has allegedly vastly overstated the legality of FSD usage and charged customers for it nonetheless. Now, tens of thousands of Korean Tesla owners are looking for answers.

Tesla apparently markets FSD in South Korea despite the fact that it knows the majority of its cars can't legally use the program in the country, the complaint from an advocacy group alleges. That means it can't be activated on the car. Soon, the complaint will be filed with the Korean Fair Trade Commission, a consumer protection agency, according to Reuters . Tesla will have to answer for why it marketed FSD to prospective buyers for years, even collecting the $6,726 lump-sum payment required for activation, even though it couldn't legally be used.

Currently, just 20% of Teslas registered in South Korea can legally use FSD because they're built in the U.S., according to a preliminary testimony given by Tesla Korea country manager Seo Young-deuk last month. Those specific cars meet U.S. vehicle-safety standards that South Korea recognizes as part of a free trade agreement. The thing is, most Teslas on the road in South Korea are manufactured in China, where no such agreement exists. It was only recently that Tesla started the process of obtaining FSD certification on China-made vehicles, even though it has been charging customers for the software for over three years.

Right now, it's not totally clear how many customers in South Korea bought FSD subscriptions on ineligible vehicles, but the automaker has sold over 170,000 China-made vehicles in the country since 2023, Reuters reports. The company continued to market FSD as sales of ineligible China-manufactured vehicles surged in South Korea in recent years, and last year, 99% of new Teslas sold in the country couldn't legally use FSD.

The complaint alleges that last year, Tesla promoted FSD as "coming soon" and posted a demonstration video filmed in South Korea without clearly disclosing that the tech could only be used in a tiny fraction of the vehicles it was selling, according to Reuters . The consumer advocacy group accused Tesla Korea of deceptive marketing and has asked the KFTC to issue a temporary cease-and-desist order on marketing FSD for ineligible vehicles, impose fines and refer the case to state investigators.

It may be an uphill battle, though. Just last month, a court in Seoul dismissed a lawsuit filed by Tesla owners seeking refunds for the FSD option, Reuters reports. The court rejected the claim that Tesla had failed to deliver the driver-assistance system. Instead, it put the onus of the issue on regulatory and legal restrictions that had limited the company's ability to roll out future functions.

raw_title: These Are the Coolest and Craziest Cars We Saw at SEMA 2026
title: These Are the Coolest and Craziest Cars We Saw at SEMA 2026
raw_summary: It’s impossible to grasp the size of the SEMA show until you actually experience it. There are thousands of builds created by tens of thousands of dedicated enthusiasts excited to share their passion with the world. While we would love to spend the full week delving into each and every build, there simply isn’t enough time. So, we picked a few of our early favorites from this year’s show. Hopefully, you’ll find them as endearing as we do. Kei cars are already an adorable bunch, but add in Rocket Bunny’s Pandem Pocket Bunny kit, and now you’re talking best-in-show cute at your local car show. What you’re looking at here is a pair of Suzuki Twins built into R32 and R34 GT-Rs. These specific examples were built with no expense spared. The R32 makes around 120 horsepower from its turbocharged 1.0-liter, while the R34’s Twin was left more stock. – Jack Fitzgerald

I found this chopped-up Tesla Cybertruck parked in the back corner of the Central Hall, covered in Grand Theft Auto VI and Rockstar Games branding. Somehow, with a sports car figure and a giant APR spoiler, the Cybertruck’s styling looks good? – Carter Fry
Can’t help but grin looking at this track-spec first-gen Toyota Tacoma . Not pictured is the engine mounted out back in the bed, below the massive rear wing. – Carter Fry

No, you’re not looking at some AI hallucination of a Lexus pickup that doesn’t exist. This is the Meso Customs TX1, a legitimate Lexus pickup based on the Toyota Tacoma and built by the crew at Meso Customs. The front end takes on the look of a Lexus GX , and even the interior gets overhauled to look and feel like what you’d get from the luxury brand. – Jack Fitzgerald

There are plenty of ways to get your race car to the track, but most of them involve purpose-built haulers based on proven HD trucks. Builder Raymond Canales looked at the available options and said, “I can do better.” Then he set to work creating this tag-axle VW hauler based on the beloved Type 2, giving new meaning to its “Transporter” surname. Built specifically to transport his VW Beetle race car, the Type 2 Hauler is just the kind of inspired lunacy with a practical purpose that we can get behind. – Andrew Wendler

Mark Denlinger’s Mad Customs is responsible for this Chevy wagon build. While Nomads get most of the love, this 210 four-door wagon restomod features a natural patina to complement its subtle hardware updates. Yes, it’s lowered, but so deftly it almost appears to just be sitting on a worn suspension; the Forgeline EO1 wheels are painted black to keep a low profile; keep the hood closed, and you’d never see its LT4 GM V-8. Denlinger also fabbed up custom tubs to clear the rear tires and modified the cargo floor to clear the custom exhaust that was crafted in-house. With apologies to Michael Jackson, this is one smooth criminal—if you know where to look. – Andrew Wendler

Steve Stroppe has a history of clean builds, and this Z/28 does nothing to sully that legacy. Featuring a carbureted Chevy big-block and a massaged turbo-hydromantic 400 transmission with a Gear Vendors overdrive, it pays respect to builds of the past. But the craftsmanship is so meticulous, and the Ice Gray Metallic paint and Graphite Blue interior are so sublime, the whole thing makes a contemporary statement without trying too hard. The Camaro was basically the poster child for custom builds in the ‘80s and ‘90s, but for those of us raised in the Rust Belt, there’s still something special about a well-executed 1969 Z/28 project. – Andrew Wendler

raw_title: GM Recalls Over 67,000 Chevy Blazer EVs And Cadillac Lyriqs, Vistiqs, And Even Celestiqs For Temporary Loss Of Braking
title: Urgent Safety Alert: GM Recalls Over 67,000 Chevy Blazer EVs And Cadillac Lyriqs, Vistiqs, And Even Celestiqs For Temporary Loss Of Braking
raw_summary: General Motors is recalling 67,380 Chevrolet Blazer EVs And Cadillac Lyriqs , Vistiqs , and even Celestiqs because under specific circumstances, a software defect can cause a temporary loss of braking ability. According to the NHTSA recall report , GM is aware of 20 minor accidents due to the fault, two of which resulted in minor injuries. Fortunately, the condition only arises at low speeds, but any loss of braking is a deeply concerning and dangerous occurrence. Two-wheel-drive Cadillac Lyriqs are not included in the recall, and the only Blazer EV trims involved are SS and Police Pursuit Vehicles. Cadillac Lyriqs are hit hardest by the recall, which includes 474 2023 Lyriqs, 22,819 2024 Lyriqs, 11,926 2025 Lyriqs, 9,322 2026 Lyriqs, and 44 2027 Lyriqs. The recall also includes 13,627 2026 Vistiqs and 5,175 2027 Vistiqs, as well as 51 2025 Celestiqs, and 31 2026 Celestiqs. (This is one of our best glimpses yet into how many Celestiqs have been sold.) The only Chevrolets included in the recall are 562 2024 Blazer EVs, 2012 2025 Blazer EVs, 1,314 2026 Blazer EVs, and 23 2027 Blazer EVs. VINs are already searchable on NHTSA's website , and the remedy comes in the form of an over-the-air update for owners who have opted in to those, otherwise owners will have to take their vehicles to dealerships to have the software update downloaded.

article_paragraphs: General Motors is recalling 67,380 Chevrolet Blazer EVs And Cadillac Lyriqs , Vistiqs , and even Celestiqs because under specific circumstances, a software defect can cause a temporary loss of braking ability. According to the NHTSA recall report , GM is aware of 20 minor accidents due to the fault, two of which resulted in minor injuries. Fortunately, the condition only arises at low speeds, but any loss of braking is a deeply concerning and dangerous occurrence. Two-wheel-drive Cadillac Lyriqs are not included in the recall, and the only Blazer EV trims involved are SS and Police Pursuit Vehicles.

Cadillac Lyriqs are hit hardest by the recall, which includes 474 2023 Lyriqs, 22,819 2024 Lyriqs, 11,926 2025 Lyriqs, 9,322 2026 Lyriqs, and 44 2027 Lyriqs. The recall also includes 13,627 2026 Vistiqs and 5,175 2027 Vistiqs, as well as 51 2025 Celestiqs, and 31 2026 Celestiqs. (This is one of our best glimpses yet into how many Celestiqs have been sold.) The only Chevrolets included in the recall are 562 2024 Blazer EVs, 2012 2025 Blazer EVs, 1,314 2026 Blazer EVs, and 23 2027 Blazer EVs. VINs are already searchable on NHTSA's website , and the remedy comes in the form of an over-the-air update for owners who have opted in to those, otherwise owners will have to take their vehicles to dealerships to have the software update downloaded.

The conditions that lead to the temporary loss of brake function are very specific. According to the recall report and GM's testing, "when the brakes are lightly applied at low speeds during a sharp turn and the vehicle encounters a bump or depression – such as at the end of a driveway – a momentary release and reapplication of the brakes may cause the software's slip calculation to misinterpret wheel movement. In some instances, this may result in a temporary loss of braking. The phenomenon is unique to certain vehicles equipped with performance all-wheel drive (pAWD, RPO X0E) and is resolved when the brakes are applied again."

GM already recalled 21,469 all-wheel-drive Lyriqs for a similar issue in 2024 , but it found that vehicles built with the software changes following that recall and vehicles that already received the software update from that recall are still susceptible to the conditions described in the new recall, and they need the latest update. The latest software update corrects the slip calculation in the vehicle's brake system control module that causes the temporary loss of braking, which coincidentally is the same claim made on the 2024 recall. Hopefully this time it actually fixes the problem.

If you drive one of the cars included in the recall, be aware of the possibility of braking loss, and remember that if you experience braking loss, normal brake function should return on the next brake press. Dealers should already be notified of the recall, but owner notification is estimated to begin on December 14.

article_paragraphs: Oh, that's just $1 million worth of vehicles driving up those ramps

SEMA is one of the few places where a Lamborghini can struggle to stand out. Park one next to a row of wildly modified trucks, and it might barely earn a second glance. Elevation Off Grid (EOG) had a different idea, and frankly, it leverages the Lamborghini in question as more of a prop since the company is really selling the Super Duty trucks it's sitting on. So yeah, this is a sincerely impressive display for multiple reasons.

First, let's break this down a touch. Elevation Off Grid is known for building custom heavy-duty trucks that don't sacrifice their heavy-duty capabilities. EOG created a similar display at SEMA in the past, but with the Lamborghini thrown in the mix, the company estimates there's close to a $1 million elevated 11 feet off the Las Vegas Convention Center floor. Watching the setup of this display is what caught our eye in the first place. Some companies may have used some type of crane or forklift, but once the Lamborghini was loaded onto the Super Duty, ramps were used to drive the car-hauling rig atop the other two shot trucks. We can only imagine that a very confident — and well-insured — driver was piloting that white Ford Super Duty .

Sure, the stunt is cool, and again, it'll get the brand noticed, but there's a somewhat sad detail why this SEMA display caught our eye in the first place. For all the cool stuff we see at SEMA each year, plenty of the cars, trucks, and SUVs in question are little more than fancy rollers. Some don't even have complete powertrains, while others are running Bluetooth driveshafts. While they might look cool, they're often held together with hopes and dreams, and the flashier vehicles tend to be vaporware cars that you could only wish to life .

That's a big reason why this demo from EOG is so cool. Any company can talk a big game, but some actually back their products up. Very few can build a truck that shows off so many concurrent skills in one relatively simple-looking display. Driving a pickup onto ramps is ordinarily unremarkable. Doing it with a Lamborghini behind the cab and two other trucks waiting underneath adds a little more pressure to the job. This all could've been viral for a very different reason.

Then consider what the other two trucks are doing — they're supporting the weight of a custom Super Duty and a Lamborghini. Yes, they're sharing the load, but we're still talking about several thousand pounds on each pickup. The company boasts that its beds are capable of supporting 10,000 pounds (4,536 kg), so in theory, each is doing relatively light work. EOG then uses LiquidSpring Smart Suspension components to keep either truck from squatting under the load. It's a very clever way to make a very clear point.

raw_title: BMW Just Went 186 MPH In The New Alpina 7 Series
title: BMW Just Went 186 MPH In The New Alpina 7 Series
raw_summary: Thanks to spy shots, we already knew BMW was hard at work cooking up the next Alpina B7 and that it'll have a V8 that sounds pretty great . The brand has now come out with official footage of the car doing high-speed testing at the Nardò test track, exceeding 186 mph. What, did you think the special label version of BMW's flagship sedan would be slow? For reference, the last-gen Alpina B7 already had a top speed of 205 mph, so 186 was frankly table stakes. That said, the speed itself arguably isn't what BMW is flexing her — it's the peace with which that speed is achieved. "Speed has always been baked into the Alpina brand's DNA," said BMW Alpina vice president Oliver Viellechner. "However, we are not just interested in top speed alone. What matters is how natural, stable and confident it feels to drive at that speed." Internally, the brand apparently calls these cars "distance-shrinking" machines; autobahn weapons made to cover literal continents in great speed, style, and serenity.

What matters is how natural, stable and confident it feels to drive at that speed." Internally, the brand apparently calls these cars "distance-shrinking" machines; autobahn weapons made to cover literal continents in great speed, style, and serenity.

You might recognize the name Nardò, by the way, from "Nardo Gray," that primer-like paint color popularized by Audi. The Nardò Ring, a 7.8-mile test track in southern Italy owned by Porsche and shaped like a perfect circle, is where that comes from.

Other confirmed details now include Alpina-signature 20-spoke lightweight wheels (peeping at the sidewall shows a diameter of 22 inches) wearing specially made tires that feature an extra layer of foam inside allowing for peak high-speed stability and comfort. Four oval exhaust tips emit a "rich, deep sound," and BMW says max torque out of that V8 is available "across virtually the entire rev range," while engine management software and throttle mapping is tweaked for smoothness over aggression. Gearbox tuning, too, has been revised to accommodate the bump in horsepower and engine speeds.

This new B7 (or whatever BMW will choose to call the next Alpina-ized 7 Series) will be the first production car made under the joint BMW Alpina brand. BMW announced that it had acquired Alpina back in 2022, but didn't take full control over the tuner until the beginning of this year. The new BMW Alpina 7 Series will be unveiled next year.

article_paragraphs: Range Rover is pulling the plug on its two most affordable models, the Evoque and Velar, as a new entry-level EV steps in.
For decades, the Range Rover name was viewed as a status symbol, mostly used by wealthy buyers, high-powered executives, and even royalty.
That started to change with the launch of the Evoque in 2011 and the Velar in 2017, making the iconic British luxury brand a little more accessible.

In the US, the 2026 Range Rover Evoque starts at $49,900, and the Velar starts at $61,600. That’s considerably less than the Sport and flagship Range Rover SUVs, which start at $83,700 and $107,400, respectively.

Range Rover’s accessible luxury era is reportedly drawing to a close. Martin Limbert, Range Rover’s managing director, confirmed to Autocar that the Evoque and Velar will officially be discontinued, with production set to end in 2027.
While it has no direct replacement planned, the new Range Rover GT will serve as the brand’s new entry-level vehicle.
Range Rover revealed the GT in July, presenting it as the fifth and newest member of the lineup. Unlike the distinct SUV design Range Rover has built the brand on, the GT is a low-slung grand tourer.
The electric GT is “a captivating new expression” of the brand, Range said, describing it as “the most technologically sophisticated” model it’s ever designed.
